TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.claim: Exalting God from what is unfit prepares for knowledge of His perfection; this passage names that prerequisite because it describes qualities leading believers to His light.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.anchor: والآية في مقام بيان خصالهم التي تستدعي هدايتهم إلى نوره فلا جرم اقتصر فيها بذكر ما هي المقدمة وهو التسبيح

TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r1.claim: A report applies the lamp parable to the believer: his heart's light nearly shines even before he speaks, and obligations and sunna illuminate one another.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r1.anchor: يكاد النور الذي في قلبه يضيء وإن لم يتكلم

TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r2.claim: The report lists five lights for the believer: entry, departure, knowledge, speech, and final arrival in paradise.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r2.anchor: فالمؤمن يتقلب في خمسة من النور مدخله نور، ومخرجه نور، وعلمه نور، وكلامه نور

TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.claim: The Prophet and his purified household are among the finest applications of the verse; its apparent scope includes other prophets, successors, and saints, but not every believer because its described qualities are not universal.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.anchor: فالآية تعم بظاهرها غيرهم من الأنبياء عليهم السلام والأوصياء والأولياء

TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك وبريدة
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r4.claim: A report says the houses God commanded to be raised are the houses of prophets; the Prophet calls Ali and Fatima's house one of the best. Al-Tabataba'i treats it as an application, also transmitted mursal in al-Majma and through Jabir from Abu Ja'far in al-Qummi.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك وبريدة قالا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.claim: The parable contrasts believers, whose hearts shine inwardly and outwardly, with unbelievers, surrounded by darkness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.anchor: hearts which have faith in them shine both inwardly and outwardly.

SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.claim: A definite noun can replace an indefinite one to identify it, as in مررت برجل عبد الله; the Quranic صراط مستقيم صراط الله gives the same construction.
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.anchor: إنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله

SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.claim: After مررت بقوم, coordinated definite names may stand in apposition; nominative is strong because it leaves the intended meaning intact.
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.anchor: أيضا مررت بقوم عبد الله وزيد وخالد والرفع جيد

SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.claim: A definite noun can replace another definite noun either to correct a mistaken first name or to shift the intended reference to the second.
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.anchor: التي تكون بدلا من المعرفة فهو كقولك مررت بعبد الله زيد

SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.claim: A phrase after an initial statement can be a new predicate answering an implied question: مهلهل's أخوالنا وهم بنو الأعمام and مررت بعبد الله أخوك illustrate it.
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.anchor: مررت بعبد الله أخوك كأنه قيل له من هو

SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.claim: الأسد شدة after رجل can raise his status as an appositive or restart as an answer to ما هو; it is not an adjective, since definite and indefinite nouns cannot modify one another.
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.anchor: كأنك قلت مررت برجل كامل لأنك أردت أن ترفع شأنه

SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.claim: Independent predication is especially strong in partitive clarification; the usage أخوالنا is good Arabic and has a parallel in an indefinite description.
SIBAWAYH:أمابدلالمعرفةمنالنكرةفقولكمررتب.anchor: وهذا عربي جيد قوله أخوالنا وقد جاء في النكرة

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r1.claim: First parse: fī buyūt is an adjective of the niche, meaning a niche in a house of God.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها صفة ل " مشكاة " أي: كمشكاة في بيوت

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r2.claim: Second parse makes fī buyūt an adjective of the lamp.

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r3.claim: Third parse makes fī buyūt an adjective of the glass.

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r4.claim: Fourth parse attaches it to tūqadu; the first four parses do not allow a pause at ʿalīm.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r4.anchor: الرابع: أنه متعلق ب " توقد ". وعلى هذه الأقوال

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r5.claim: Fifth parse connects the phrase to an omitted verb, as in the phrase about nine signs: He is glorified in houses; this allows pausing at ʿalīm.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r5.anchor: الخامس: أنه متعلق بمحذوف كقوله في تسع آيات

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r6.claim: Sixth parse attaches it to yusabbiḥ, so men glorify God in houses; the repeated fīhā is emphatic, as in the cited verse, and a pause at ʿalīm is possible.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r6.anchor: وفيها تكرير للتوكيد كقوله: ففي الجنة خالدين فيها

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r7.claim: Al-Samīn notes that al-Shaykh says there are three such parses but actually names only two.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r7.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وعلى هذه الأقوال الثلاثة " ولم يذكر سوى قولين

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r8.claim: The clause with adhina Allāh is an adjective of buyūt; an is preceded by an omitted preposition, as though it said fī an turfaʿ.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r8.anchor: في محل جر صفة ل " بيوت "

SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r9.claim: Fī buyūt cannot attach to yudhkar, because that verb is coordinated inside the complement of an, and material after an cannot be moved before it.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36/r9.anchor: ولا يجوز تعلق " في بيوت " بقوله: " ويذكر "

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read yusabbaḥu with fatḥa on bāʾ, in the passive; one of the three genitive phrases becomes deputy subject, with the first preferred because the verb needs a nominative and it is nearer.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر بفتح الباء مبنيا للمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r4.speaker: باقي السبعة
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r4.claim: The other canonical readers use active yusabbiḥu with kasra on bāʾ, making rijāl the subject; there is then no pause at al-āṣāl.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r4.anchor: وباقي السبعة بكسر الباء مبنيا للفاعل. والفاعل " رجال "

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r5.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r5.claim: Ibn Waththāb and Abū Ḥaywa read tusabbiḥu with feminine tāʾ and active kasra, since a broken plural can take feminine agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وأبو حيوة " تسبح " بالتاء من فوق

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar uses the same feminine tāʾ but passive fatḥa; al-Zamakhsharī parses the times as subject with an extra bāʾ, while others make glorification the implied deputy subject, figuratively attributed to those times.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر كذلك إلا أنه فتح الباء

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r7.claim: Al-Samīn prefers the implied tasbīḥa as deputy subject: glorification is metaphorically attributed to morning and evening, and this fits better than the cited al-Jāthiya example because no explicit object occurs here.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r7.anchor: وخرجها غيره على أن القائم مقام الفاعل ضمير التسبيحة

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r8.claim: The al-Jāthiya reading is parsed as an implied al-jazāʾ, the recompense, being given to a people.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r8.anchor: كما خرجوا قراءة أبي جعفر أيضا { ليجزى قوما بما كانوا يكسبون }

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r1.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r1.claim: The tafsir takes أن ترفع to mean that the houses are built; these houses are mosques, with في linked to the preceding comparison to a niche.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r1.anchor: و" في " من صلة قوله (كمشكاة). المعنى كمشكاة في بيوت، أي في مساجد.

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r2.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets أن ترفع as meaning that the houses are honored and exalted.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: تأويل " أن ترفع " أن تعظم.

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r3.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the houses refer to the Jerusalem sanctuary.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن يعني به بيت المقدس

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r4.claim: Alternatively, في attaches to يسبح; فيها is then repeated for emphasis, yielding the sense that men glorify God in houses ordained to be raised.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون " في " متصلة ب (يسبح) ويكون فيها تكريرا على التوكيد، فيكون المعنى يسبح لله رجال

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r5.claim: With يُسبح read in the passive, رجال is nominative as the deputy subject.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r5.anchor: وتقرأ (يسبح) له فيها، فيكون رفع رجال ههنا على تفسير ما لم يسم فاعله،

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r6.claim: The poet's construction ليبك يزيد ضارع supports the passive verb followed by a nominative subject.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r6.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة. . . ومختبط مما تطيح الطوائح

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r7.claim: The singular of الآصال is أصل, and it means evenings.

ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r1.claim: Asad supplies an implied "ordained" in the literal rendering of the clause about God's name being remembered in the houses.

ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r2.claim: The sequence implies that the spiritual purpose of worship houses is fulfilled by only some of their habitual congregants.
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n56/r2.anchor: the spiritual purpose of those houses of worship is fulfilled only by some, and not all, of the people who are wont to congregate in them out of habit.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r7.claim: The phrase “in houses” is grammatically connected to “niche.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r8.claim: These are places of worship, not idol-worship or liquor-drinking venues; the lamp signifies an upright believer’s heart, which is found among believers in God’s mosques.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r8.anchor: This niche is found in places where God is worshipped.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r9.speaker: Al-Zamakhsharī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers connecting “in houses” with the niche, reading the verse as locating these illuminated believers in mosques.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r9.anchor: Al-Zamakhshar ī has given preference to this view.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r10.claim: The verb rafaʿa here means to build or construct, as in the account of Abraham building the foundations of the House.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r10.anchor: here means to build and construct. A similar usage of this word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r11.claim: Dhikr includes prayer and every other form of remembrance of God, including acts undertaken to raise the banner of His religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p333/r11.anchor: encompasses the prayer as well all other forms of God’s remembrance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r1.claim: These houses primarily mean worship places built at God's direct command: the Kaʿbah by Abraham and Ishmael and Bayt al-Maqdis by Solomon, with their branches included; idolatrous shrines are excluded as abodes of filth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r1.anchor: their foremost connotations are the worship places that were built as a result of His direct command

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.claim: After the faith parable names mosques, the discourse describes how believers live; it states the effect after its cause so faith is personified in lived conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.anchor: This is like stating the effect after stating the cause so that a fact can be personified in real life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r3.claim: The phrase for morning and evening means day and night, as in ordinary language.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r3.anchor: has the same meaning as that of “day and night” in our language.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r1.speaker: عاصم برواية أبي بكر وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r1.claim: Asim in Abu Bakr's narration and Ibn Amir read yusabbaḥ with fatḥa on bāʾ, a passive form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: (يسبح) بفتح الباء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r2.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r2.claim: The other readers, including Hafs from Asim, read yusabbiḥ with kasra on bāʾ, the active form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: يسبح بكسر الباء، وكذلك حفص عن عاصم أيضا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r3.speaker: أحمد بن أبي خيثمة وإدريس بن عبد الكريم وبكار عن أبان
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r3.claim: Transmitters from Asim through al-Dahhak and Aban also report the kasra reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r3.anchor: حدثني أحمد بن أبي خيثمة وإدريس بن عبد الكريم جميعا عن خلف عن الضحاك بن ميمون عن عاصم يسبح بكسر الباء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r4.claim: With fatḥa, the prepositional phrase is promoted to subject and an implicit subject is then understood; رجال explicates who performs the glorification, as in the poem لبيك يزيد ضارع لخصومة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r4.anchor: من قال: (يسبح له فيها) ففتح الباء فعلى أنه أقام الجار والمجرور مقام الفاعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r5.claim: The kasra reading is preferable: رجال is the direct subject of yusabbiḥ, further described by لا تلهيهم تجارة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p325#2/r5.anchor: والوجه يسبح، كما قرأه الجمهور، فيكون فاعل يسبح رجال الموصوفون بقوله: لا تلهيهم تجارة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r1.claim: With fatḥa on bāʾ, the verb is passive; al-rijāl is a nominative topic and لا تلهيهم its predicate.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بفتح الباء وكسرها فالحجة لمن فتح أنه جعله فعلا لما لم يسم فاعله ورفع الرجال بالابتداء والخبر لا تلهيهم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r2.claim: With kasra on bāʾ, the men perform the verb, and the following words describe their state.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p262#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن كسر أنه جعله فعلا للرجال فرفعهم به وجعل ما بعدهم وصفا لحالهم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r9.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read yusabbiḥ with kasra on bāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r9.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائى وحفص عن عاصم ﴿ يسبح ﴾ بكسر الباء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r10.speaker: خلف عن الضحاك بن ميمون عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r10.claim: Idrīs and Aḥmad b. Abī Khaythama transmit the kasra reading of yusabbiḥ from ʿĀṣim through Khalaf and al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. Maymūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r10.anchor: حدثنى إدريس بن عبد الكريم وأحمد بن أبى خيثمة جميعا عن خلف عن الضحاك بن ميمون عن عاصم ﴿ يسبح ﴾ بكسر الباء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r11.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r11.speaker: بكار عن أبان عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r11.claim: Bakkār transmits the kasra reading of yusabbiḥ from ʿĀṣim through Abān.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r11.anchor: وروى بكار عن أبان عن عاصم ﴿ يسبح ﴾ أيضا بكسر الباء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r12.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r12.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r12.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr read yusabbiḥ with fatḥa on bāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p455/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر ﴿ يسبح ﴾ بفتح الباء

NASHR:v2p428/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p428/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p428/r1.claim: The author found no explicit ruling for takbīr at Qurʾān completion among the Shāfiʿīs beyond the material already cited, nor among the Ḥanafīs or Mālikīs; Ibn Mufliḥ records two Hanbalī reports, one recommending it from al-Ḍuḥā or Alam Nashraḥ to each sūra’s end, while another excludes readers other than Ibn Kathīr and mentions tahlīl.
NASHR:v2p428/r1.anchor: لم أر للحنفية، ولا للمالكية، وأما الحنابلة فقال الفقيه الكبير أبو عبد الله محمد بن مفلح

NASHR:v2p428/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p428/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p428/r2.claim: During Ramadan in Mecca, the author observed everyone leading tarāwīḥ in the Sacred Mosque use takbīr from al-Ḍuḥā at completion, which he takes as evidence that the sunna continues there.
NASHR:v2p428/r2.anchor: فلم أر أحدا ممن صلى التراويح بالمسجد الحرام إلا يكبر من الضحى عند الختم فعلمت أنها سنة باقية

NASHR:v2p428/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p428/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p428/r3.claim: The author criticizes denying takbīr despite reports from the Prophet, Companions, and Successors while permitting the tasbīḥ prayer despite most hadith specialists not authenticating its report.
NASHR:v2p428/r3.anchor: ثم العجب ممن ينكر التكبير بعد ثبوته عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وعن أصحابه

NASHR:v2p428/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p428/r4.speaker: القاضي حسين
NASHR:v2p428/r4.claim: Several jurists recommend the tasbīḥ prayer on the basis of its report, including al-Qāḍī Ḥusayn, the authors of al-Tahdhīb and al-Tatimma, al-Rūyānī, and al-Mubārak; the report is also cited by Ḥanafī authorities.
NASHR:v2p428/r4.anchor: فقال القاضي الحسين، وصاحب التهذيب والتتمة والروياني في أواخر كتاب الجنائز من كتاب البحر

QIRAAT-ER:24:36:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:36:2#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:24:36:2#1/r1.claim: The variant has kasra rather than ḍamma on bāʾ, a dialectal plural vocalization with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:24:36:2#1/r1.anchor: vw, mutawatir: Kasra on bāʾ instead of ḍamma — dialectal variant in plural vocalization; no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:24:36:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:36:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:24:36:11#1/r1.claim: The passive yusabbaḥu means “He is glorified” rather than active “glorifies”; it removes an explicit agent and makes the spaces a locus of praise.
QIRAAT-ER:24:36:11#1/r1.anchor: the spaces themselves become locus of impersonal praise

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the houses God commanded to be raised as mosques and explains raising them as honoring them for God’s remembrance.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ﴾ قال هي المساجد ﴿ أذن الله أن ترفع ﴾ يقول أن تعظم لذكره

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the mosques are to be built for God and used for prayer in the morning and evening.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ﴾ قال هي المساجد ﴿ أذن الله أن ترفع ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r3.speaker: أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r3.claim: Companions of the Prophet said mosques are God’s houses on earth, and God honors those who visit them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق عن عمرو بن ميمون الأودي قال أدركت أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم يقولون إن المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r3.claim: The apparent sense is the generic plural: houses as a class.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله في بيوت أريد به مدلوله من الجمعية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the houses as the Jerusalem sanctuary, called plural because it contains distinct, partitioned spaces.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: أريد به بيت المقدس، وسمي بيوتا من حيث فيه مواضع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r5.claim: The account says the Israelites carefully maintained its lamps with specially prepared, sanctified oil sealed in its containers, which made the light brighter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r5.anchor: ويؤثر أن عادة بني إسرائيل في وقيده في غاية التهمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r6.claim: The generic wording covers mosques and houses where prayer and learning take place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن في بيوت مطلق فيصدق على المساجد والبيوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r7.claim: Mujāhid identifies the houses as the homes of the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بيوت الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid identify them as mosques customarily lit with this type of lamp.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن أيضا ومجاهد: هي المساجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r9.claim: Another view identifies the houses as the Kaʿba, Jerusalem sanctuary, the Prophet's mosque, and Qubāʾ mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r9.anchor: وقيل: الكعبة وبيت المقدس ومسجد الرسول عليه الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r10.claim: Another view identifies them as the houses of the prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r10.anchor: وقيل: بيوت الأنبياء. ويقوي أنها المساجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r11.claim: The mention of glorification in the houses morning and evening strengthens the mosque interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r11.anchor: ويقوي أنها المساجد قوله يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r12.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk interpret raising the houses as honoring and exalting them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r12.anchor: وأمره بأن ترفع أي يعظم قدرها قاله الحسن والضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r13.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid understand this as building the houses and raising them, as Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: تبنى وتعلى من قوله وإذ يرفع إبراهيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r14.claim: Another gloss says the houses are to be purified of filth and sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r14.anchor: وقيل: ترفع تطهر من الأنجاس والمعاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r15.claim: Another gloss says needs are raised there to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r15.anchor: وقيل: ترفع أي ترفع فيها الحوائج إلى الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r16.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r16.claim: Another gloss says voices are raised there in remembrance of God and Qurʾān recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r16.anchor: وقيل: ترفع الأصوات بذكر الله وتلاوة القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r17.claim: The wording apparently covers every kind of remembrance without restriction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r17.anchor: ويذكر فيها اسمه ظاهره مطلق الذكر فيعم كل ذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains remembrance as God's oneness, namely lā ilāha illā Allāh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r18.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: توحيده وهو لا إله إلا الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says God's book is recited in the houses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r19.anchor: وعنه: يتلى فيها كتابه. وقيل: أسماؤه الحسنى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r20.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r20.claim: Another gloss takes the phrase to mean God's beautiful names.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r21.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r21.claim: Another gloss takes it to mean that prayer is performed in the houses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r21.anchor: وقيل: يصلى فيها. وقرأ الجمهور يسبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r22.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r22.claim: The majority read yusabbiḥu with kasra on bāʾ and yāʾ as its first consonant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r22.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يسبح بكسر الباء وبالياء من تحت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r23.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r23.claim: Ibn Waththāb and Abū Ḥaywa use the same vocalization but with tāʾ as the first consonant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r23.anchor: وابن وثاب وأبو حيوة كذلك إلا أنه بالتاء من فوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r24.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر والبحتري عن حفص ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو والمهال عن يعقوب والمفضل وأبان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r24.claim: These readers use fatḥa on bāʾ and yāʾ initially; one of the preceding genitives then serves as the passive subject, with the nearer one preferred because the verb selects its subject more strongly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r24.anchor: وابن عامر وأبو بكر والبحتري عن حفص ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r25.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r25.speaker: أبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r25.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads tusabbaḥ with tāʾ initially and fatḥa on bāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r25.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: تسبح بالتاء من فوق وفتح الباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the passive reading by treating the morning and evening times as the subject, with an additional bāʾ, so that the times themselves are glorified.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ووجهها أن تسند إلى أوقات الغدو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān also allows an implicit verbal noun, tasbīḥa, to serve as the passive subject, as in the passive reading of li-yujzā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله ضمير التسبيحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.speaker: أبو مجلز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r3.claim: Abū Mujliz reads al-īṣāl in place of al-āṣāl.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase في بيوت attaches to يسبح; its repetition as فيها emphasizes and recalls what follows, and fronting signals importance rather than restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.anchor: بيسبح وفيها تكرير لذلك جيء به للتأكيد والتذكير بما بعد في الجملة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.claim: Some grammarians call the repeated phrase بدل; al-Mughni calls it emphasis of the preposition by repeating it with an attached pronoun. Al-Alusi objects that explicit wording is stronger and cannot be emphasized by a pronoun; some allow بدل by analogy, and he answers that the whole phrase may be بدل or emphasis with an explicit form to avoid repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.anchor: وبعض النحاة أعرب نحو ذلك بدلا كما في شرح التسهيل وفي المغنى هو من توكيد الحرف بإعادة ما دخل عليه مضمرا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.claim: رجال is the subject of يسبح and follows the circumstantial phrase because its lengthy description would disrupt the verse's smooth order if placed earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.anchor: رجال ( الخ استئناف لبيان حال من حصلت لهم الهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r4.speaker: الرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r4.claim: Al-Rummani attaches في بيوت to يوقد.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r4.anchor: وقال الرماني في بيوت ) متعلق بيوقد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r5.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r5.claim: Al-Hawfi makes في بيوت an omitted phrase functioning as an adjective of مشكاة; others make it an adjective of مصباح or زجاجة. These analyses restrict the parable to its exemplar and take the tanwin as denoting a kind, not an individual.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحوفي : متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة لمشكاة وقيل هو صفة لمصباح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi rejects those four attachments as unsuitable: the parable plainly continues through 24:35, and inserting the beneficiaries' state as an aside would improperly interrupt it while opponents' state is central.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r6.anchor: بعد قوله تعالى ( ولو لم تمسسه نار ) على ما هو الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r7.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r7.claim: Al-Khafaji calls the objection ornate nonsense and says there is no interruption: the parable ends at ولو لم تمسسه نار (24:35). Another view ends it at نور على نور and takes يسبحوا as omitted, with the clause consequential without a فاء.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r7.anchor: وتعقبه الخفاجي بأنه زخرف من القول إذ لا فصل فيه وما قبله إلى هنا من المثل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r8.claim: A proposed implicit يسبحوا makes the clause follow from the preceding one without a فاء, like قم يدعوك; attachment to يذكر is ruled out because يذكر is governed by أن and cannot govern a preceding phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r8.anchor: وقيل هو بسبحوا أو نحوه محذوفا وتلك الجملة على ما قيل مترتبة على ما قبلها وترك الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Mujahid identify the houses as all mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r9.anchor: والمراد بالبيوت المساجد كلها كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وقتادة ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the phrase to four mosques built by prophets: the Kaaba by Abraham and Ishmael, Jerusalem by David and Solomon, and Medina and Quba by Muhammad; al-Alusi says this is far from the apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن زيد أنه قال : إنما هي أربع مساجد يبنهن إلا نبي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the houses as Jerusalem, using a plural because it contains distinct locations; al-Alusi also finds this far from the apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r11.anchor: وعن الحسن أن المراد بها بيت المقدس والجمع من حيث أن فيه مواضع يتميز بعضها عن بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك وبريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r1.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports that the Prophet identified these houses as prophets’ houses; when Abu Bakr asked about Ali and Fatima’s home, he said it was among the most excellent, a report al-Alusi says should stand if sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r1.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك وبريدة قال : قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the houses generally to include mosques and homes where prayer and religious learning occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الظاهر أنها مطلقة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan also allows the houses to symbolize believers’ prayers or bodies, likened to mosques; al-Alusi finds this interpretation unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بها صلاة المؤمنين أو أبدانهم بأن تشبه صلاتهم الجامعة للعبادات القولية والفعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r4.claim: Permission means God’s command, and raising the houses means honoring them; al-Alusi identifies this as the sound explanation of the phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r4.anchor: والمراد بالإذن الأمر وبالرفع التعظيم أي أمر سبحانه بتعظيم قدرها وروي هذا عن الحسن والضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r5.claim: If the houses are mosques, honoring them entails protecting them from ritual impurity and contamination: jurists prohibit entry by menstruating or postpartum women and the ritually impure, even in transit, and bar anything likely to soil them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p174/r5.anchor: إذا أريد بها المساجد فتعظيم قدرها يكون بأشياء شتى كصيانتها عن دخول الجنب والحائض والنفساء ولو على وجه العبور

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r1.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r1.claim: Ibn Majah transmits from Wathila that the Prophet instructed people to keep mosques free of children, the insane, commerce, disputes, loud voices, punishments, and drawn swords, and to provide water places and incense them on Fridays.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن ماجة عن واثلة بن الأسقع عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : جنبوا مساجدكم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r2.speaker: ثوبان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r2.claim: Thawban reports the Prophet’s instruction to rebuke people who recite poetry or announce lost property in mosques, repeating the prescribed rebuke three times.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r2.anchor: فقد أخرج الطبراني وابن السني وابن منده عن ثوبان قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r3.claim: The ban on poetry applies to blameworthy verse, such as satire of Muslims or erotic and wine poetry; verse praising prophecy or Islam, imparting wisdom, or encouraging virtue and asceticism is allowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r3.anchor: وينبغي أن يقيد المنع من إنشاد الشعر بما إذا كان فيه شيء مذموم كهجو المسلم وصفة الخمر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r4.speaker: رجل من الأنصار
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r4.claim: A Companion from the Ansar reports that anyone finding a louse in a mosque should wrap it in his garment and remove it after leaving.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r4.anchor: عن رجل من الأنصار قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : إذا وجد أحدكم القملة في المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r5.claim: Discarding a killed louse in a mosque is mildly disliked, and a live one should not be left there; urinating there is forbidden even into a container.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r5.anchor: ومنع إلقاء القملة فيه بعد قتلها وهو مكروه تنزيها على ما صرح به بعض المتأخرين ويندب أن لا تلقى حية في المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r6.claim: Al-Alusi has not found an explicit ruling on bloodletting into a container in a mosque, but says it should be treated like urination because both urine and blood are gravely impure.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r6.anchor: وفي الأشباه وأما الفصد في المسجد في إناء فلم أره وينبغي أن لا فرق أي لأن كلا من البول والدم نجس مغلظ

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r7.claim: Spitting and bodily mucus must be kept out of mosques; ablution there is disliked as naturally repugnant, so mosques must be kept clean.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r7.anchor: وفي البدائع يكره التوضيء في المسجد لأنه مستقذر طبعا فيجب تنزيه المسجد عنه كما يجب تنزيهه عن المخاط والبلغم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r8.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r8.claim: Al-Shaʿbi reports that the Prophet scraped phlegm from the mosque’s qibla wall and applied perfume there, calling the act a Sunna; phlegm on top of a mat is less bad than underneath, and if unavoidable it should be buried.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن الشعبي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى في قبلة المسجد نخامة فقام إليها فحكها بيده الشريفة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r9.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r9.claim: A report from Anas says spitting in a mosque is a sin and its expiation is to cover it; al-Alusi adds that al-Tabarani transmits a similar report from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r9.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة عن أنس مرفوعا التفل في المسجد خطيئة وكفارته أن يواريه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r10.claim: Sexual intercourse and relieving oneself in or atop a mosque are forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r10.anchor: ومنع الوطء فيها وفوقها كالتخلي وصرحوا بحرمة ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r11.claim: People with odor from garlic, onions, leeks, radishes, chronic bad breath, strong body odor, or foul-smelling clothes should not enter; garlic-smelling men were led to al-Baqiʿ in the Prophet’s time.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r11.anchor: ومنع دخول من أكل ذا رائحة كريهة فيها كالثوم والبصل والكراث وأكل الفجل إذا تجشا كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r12.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r12.claim: Malik says oil-makers should stay back and not take the front rows, evidently because of their odor.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r12.anchor: وعن مالك أن الزياتين يتأخرون ولا يتقدمون أي إلى الوصف الأول ويقعدون في أخريات الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r13.claim: Eating garlic in a mosque is prohibited for anyone not in retreat; sitting there for condolences or worldly conversation is prohibited, and using a mosque as a passage is disliked or forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r13.anchor: ومنع الثوم والأكل فيها لغير معتكف ومنع الجلوس فيها للمصيبة أو للتحدث بكلام الدنيا ومنع اتخاذها طريقا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r14.claim: A report from Ibn Umar traces the prohibition on passing through mosques to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175/r14.anchor: وقد جار النهي عن ذلك في حديث رواه ابن ماجه عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that making a mosque a thoroughfare is one of the signs of the Hour; habitually doing so is sinful and makes a person publicly disobedient, while a genuine excuse removes the dislike.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن ابن مسعود أن اتخاذها طريقا من أشراط الساعة وفي القنية معتاد ذلك يأثم ويفسق

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that mosques were sprinkled and swept in the Prophet’s time.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r2.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن زيد ابن أسلم قال : كان المسجد يرش ويقم على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r3.speaker: يعقوب بن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r3.claim: Yaqub ibn Zayd reports that the Prophet removed mosque dust with a palm frond.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج عن يعقوب بن زيد أن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يتبع غبار المسجد بجريدة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r4.claim: Mosque members may furnish a mosque with brick, mats, or lamps from their own money, not mosque funds unless the ruler authorizes it, except where the endower specified this use.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r4.anchor: ولأهل المسجد أن يفرشوا المسجد بالآجر والحصير ويعلقوا القناديل لكن من مال أنفسهم لا من مال المسجد إلا بأمر الحاكم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r5.claim: Lavish lighting on set nights that draws children and idlers into noise and disrespect is a reprehensible innovation; patterned carpets that distract worshippers and diminish concentration should likewise be avoided.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r5.anchor: إيقاد القناديل الكثيرة فيها في ليالي معروفة من السنة كليلة السابع والعشرين من رمضان الموجب لاجتماع الصبيان وأهل البطالة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r6.claim: Some authorities recommend entering with the right foot, leaving with the left, and praying two rakahs before sitting when entering for a purpose other than prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r6.anchor: ومن التعظيم أيضا تقديم الرجل اليمنى عند دخولها واليسرى عند الخروج منها وصلاة الداخل ركعتين قبل الجلوس إذا كان دخوله لغير الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r7.speaker: أبو قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r7.claim: Abu Qatada reports the Prophet’s instruction to give mosques their due, explaining that this means praying two rakahs before sitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن أبي قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : اعطوا المساجد حقها قيل : وما حقها قال : ركعتان قبل أن تسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r8.claim: Mosques may be built high, unlike ordinary houses, but should not be decorated in ways that distract worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r8.anchor: ومن ذلك أيضا بناؤها رفيعة عالية لا كسائر البيوت لكن لا ينبغي تزيينها بما يشوش على المصلين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r9.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r9.claim: A report from Jubayr ibn Mutim says mosques should not be built with images or adorned with glass.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r9.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه ابن ماجه والطبراني عن جبير بن مطعم مرفوعا أنها لا تبنى بالتصاوير ولا تزين بالقوارير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r10.claim: Some interpret raising as constructing high buildings, citing Abraham’s raising the foundations of the House; al-Alusi prefers honoring the mosques generally, with lofty construction included among its instances.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r10.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الرفع ببنائها رفيعة كما في قوله تعالى : ( وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r11.claim: The suggestions that raising means needs being presented to God there or voices being raised in remembrance are unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : ترفع الأصوات بذكر الله عز وجل فيها ولا يخفى ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r12.claim: Calling God’s command permission hints that the person being commanded is already inclined to the commanded act, as though seeking permission to carry it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r12.anchor: إلى المأمور به قبل الأمر به ناويا لتحقيقه كأنه مستأذن في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r13.claim: The remembrance of God includes all forms of remembrance and religious learning; Ibn Abbas narrows it to monotheism or Qur’an recitation, and another view takes it as God’s beautiful names.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r13.anchor: والمراد بذكر اسمه تعالى شأنه ما يعم جميع أذكاره تعالى وجعل من ذلك المباحث العلمية المتعلقة به عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to interpret remembrance as affirming divine unity, specifically saying “There is no god but God.”
ALUSI-FULL:v18p175#2/r14.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما المراد به توحيده عز وجل وهو قول :

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r1.claim: Tasbih means declaring God transcendent and holy; it is used with or without the preposition li, as in “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.”
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r1.anchor: والتسبيح التنزيه والتقديس ويستعمل باللام وبدونها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r2.claim: Tasbih may mean its ordinary sense or prayer, since prayer contains glorification; Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak report the prayer interpretation, and Ibn Abbas says every Qur’anic tasbih means prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r2.anchor: وروي هذا عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r3.claim: The specified times support reading tasbih as prayer; dawn and evening are singled out as especially honored and as common times of work and occupation.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r3.anchor: وأيد إرادة الصلاة هنا تعيين الأوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r4.claim: Al-ghuduww can be the plural of ghada or a verbal noun used for the time; al-asal is the plural of asil, though that plural pattern is not regular, while al-asl is another analysis for evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r4.anchor: والغدو جمع غداة كفتى وفتاة أو مصدر أطلق على الوقت الغدو

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r5.speaker: مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r5.claim: Mujliz reads al-īsāl as a verbal noun meaning entering the time of evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r5.anchor: بأن مجلز قرأ ( والأيصال ) مصدرا أي الدخول في وقت الأصيل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes al-asal as the plural of asl, like neck and necks; evening extends from the sun’s decline to morning, while the two terms can also mean the beginning and end of day.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r6.anchor: واختار الزمخشري أنه جمه أصل كعنق وأعناق

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas takes al-ghadah to mean forenoon and says the forenoon prayer is mentioned in the Qur’an, reciting this verse through al-asal as evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه حمل الغداة على وقت الضحى وهو مقتضى ما أخرج ابن أبي شيبة والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r8.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر والبحتري عن حفص ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو والمنهال عن يعقوب والمفضل وأبان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r8.claim: These readers have yusabbahu in the masculine passive; its deputy subject may be lahu, fīhā, or bi-l-ghuduww, with the first preferred as nearest to the verb and a true attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر والبحتري عن حفص ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو والمنهال عن يعقوب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.claim: On the masculine passive reading, rijāl is raised either as the subject of an omitted verb or as the predicate of an omitted subject, supplying the men who glorify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.anchor: ورفع ( رجال ) على هذه القراءة على أنه فاعل لفعل محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r10.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r10.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Waththab read tasbaḥu in the feminine active, with rijāl as its subject; the feminine agreement is licensed by the broken plural’s frequent feminine treatment.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن وثاب ( تسبح ) بالتاء الفوقية والبناء للفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r11.claim: Abu Jafar reads tasbaḥu in the feminine passive, taking the times as deputy subject with an extra bāʾ and figurative attribution; Abu Hayyan instead allows an implied tasbiḥa as subject, a reading al-Alusi’s cited authority prefers.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ( تسبح ) بالتاء الفوقية والبناء للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.claim: A poetic example illustrates the accepted ellipsis of a verb or subject in this construction; many grammarians allow such ellipsis by analogy, unlike the explicitly disallowed use of an agent as a specification after a passive verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.anchor: وهذا نظير قوله : لبيك يزيد ضارع لخصومة ومختبط مما تطيح الطوائح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets remembrance as recitation of God’s Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r13.anchor: وعنه أيضا المراد تلاوة كتابه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r14.claim: Remembering God is coordinated with raising the houses as a specific instance of the general honoring of mosques, not as an explanatory apposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r14.anchor: وعطف الذكر على الرفع من قبيل عطف الخاص على العام فإن ذكر اسمه تعالى فيها من أنواع تعظيمها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.claim: On the reading discussed above, rijāl is raised as subject or predicate; its tanwin in every reading conveys magnificence.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.anchor: فرفع ( رجال ) على هذه القراءة على الفاعلية أو الخبرية كما سمعت آنفا والتنوين فيه على جميع القراءات للتفخيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r1.claim: The lamp mentioned in the parable is located in houses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r1.anchor: قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله} أي: ذلك المصباح في بيوت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the lamp is lit in the houses, which are mosques.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: يوقد في بيوت، والبيوت: هي المساجد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says mosques are God's houses on earth, shining for heaven's inhabitants as stars shine for earth's inhabitants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r3.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: "المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض، وهي تضيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r4.speaker: ابن بريدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r4.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that only four mosques were built by prophets: the Kaaba by Abraham and Ishmael as a qibla, Jerusalem by David and Solomon, Medina by the Prophet, and Quba on piety by the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p49#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن بريدة في قوله تعالى" "في بيوت أذن الله"، قال: إنما هي أربعة مساجد لم يبنها إلا نبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r1.claim: Mujahid says the houses are to be built, as in the verse about Abraham raising the foundations of the House.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: أن تبنى، نظيره قوله تعالى: "وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r2.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the houses are to be honored, with indecent speech not mentioned in them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: أي تعظم أي لا يذكر فيه الخنا من القول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains remembering God's name in the houses as reciting His Book.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يتلى فيها كتابه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r4.claim: Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read yusabbahu with a fatḥa on the ba in the passive, pausing at al-asal; the others read yusabbihu with kasra, making the men the agents of glorification.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر "يسبح" بفتح الباء على غير تسمية الفاعل، والوقف على هذه القراءة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r5.anchor: جعلوا التسبيح فعلا للرجال، {يسبح له} أي: يصلي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r6.claim: Exegetes take morning and evening glorification as the obligatory prayers: dawn is Fajr, while al-asal encompasses noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r6.anchor: قال أهل التفسير: أراد به الصلوات المفروضات. فالتي تؤدى بالغداة صلاة الصبح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r7.claim: Another view limits the prayers meant to Fajr and Asr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r7.anchor: وقيل: أراد به صلاة الصبح والعصر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r8.claim: The Prophet says that whoever prays the two cool-time prayers enters Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r8.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من صلى البردين دخل الجنة"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the morning glorification with the forenoon prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: التسبيح بالغدو صلاة الضحى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r10.speaker: أبو أمامة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r10.claim: Abu Umama reports that walking in purity to an obligatory prayer earns the reward of a pilgrim in ihram; walking solely for the forenoon prayer earns the reward of one performing umra; and prayer after prayer without idle speech is recorded in Illiyyin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p50/r10.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من مشى إلى صلاة مكتوبة وهو متطهر فأجره كأجر الحاج المحرم

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r1.claim: Fī buyūt may attach to the preceding parable as a niche in some houses, or to the lamp being kindled in houses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r1.anchor: متعلق بما قبله أي كمشكاة في بعض بيوت

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r2.claim: Attaching it to kindling restricts the example to a fine setting, since mosque lamps are larger; it may instead depict believers' prayers or bodies as mosques.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r2.anchor: تقييد للممثل به بما يكون تحبيرا ومبالغة فيه فإن قناديل المساجد تكون أعظم

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r3.claim: Plural houses do not conflict with one niche, which denotes a type without specifying number.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r3.anchor: ولا ينافي جمع البيوت وحدة المشكاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r4.claim: Alternatively, it attaches to yusabbiḥ or an implied command to pray in houses; it cannot attach to yudhkar because the latter is governed by an.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r4.anchor: أو بما بعده وهو يسبح، وفيها تكرير مؤكد

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r5.claim: The houses are mosques, whose qualities suit the description; some say the three mosques, with indefiniteness for glorification.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r5.anchor: والمراد بها المساجد لأن الصفة تلائمها

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r6.claim: God permitted the houses to be raised in construction or elevated through honor.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r7.claim: Remembering God's name includes mention of His acts and discussion of His rulings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r7.anchor: عام فيما يتضمن ذكره حتى المذاكرة في أفعاله

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r8.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent and here refers to prayer in mornings and evenings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r8.anchor: ينزهونه أي يصلون له فيها بالغدوات والعشيات

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r9.claim: Ghudu is a verbal noun used for morning time, paired with āṣāl, the plural of aṣīl.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r9.anchor: والغدو مصدر أطلق للوقت ولذلك حسن اقترانه بالآصال

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r10.claim: A reading has al-īṣāl, meaning entry into the evening.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r10.anchor: وهو جمع أصيل، وقرىء «والإيصال» وهو الدخول في الأصيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r11.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read yusabbiḥ with fatḥa, assigning it to a time expression and raising rijāl by implication.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر «يسبح» بالفتح على إسناده إلى أحد الظروف الثلاثة

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r12.claim: The verb is also read tusabbiḥ with kasra for feminine plural agreement, or with fatḥa assigned to morning times.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:36/r12.anchor: وقرىء تسبح بالتاء مكسورا لتأنيث الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r1.claim: The plural houses means the walls of houses and indicates that the niche is a general kind, not a single one; the singularity of its light fittings signals its great rarity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r1.anchor: دلالة على أن المراد بالمشكاة الجنس لا الواحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r2.claim: God's permission means He enables, permits, recommends, or makes obligatory; raising the houses is physical in construction and spiritual through sincere good works.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r2.anchor: حسا في البناء , ومعنى بإخلاصها للعمل الصالح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r3.claim: Abū Dāwūd reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that the Prophet sought refuge in God when entering a mosque; ʿUqba ibn Muslim adds that Satan then says the person is protected for the day. The author gives no grading.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r4.claim: God's name is remembered there by any person He permits, in remembrance free of admixture or deceit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r4.anchor: أي ذكرا صافيا عن شوب , وخالصا عن غش

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r5.claim: Yusabbiḥu here means both praying and declaring God transcendent, and the worship is for Him alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r5.anchor: فيها بالغدو } أي الإبكار , بصلاة الصبح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r6.claim: Dawn denotes the morning prayer and evenings denote the remaining prayers; beginning and ending their work with remembrance preserves and blesses the intervening activity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r6.anchor: ويختمونها بذكره ليحفظوا فيما بين ذلك ويبارك لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r7.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r7.claim: Al-Baghawī says the plural al-āṣāl includes ẓuhr, ʿaṣr, maghrib, and ʿishāʾ.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r7.anchor: قال البغوي : لأن اسم الأصيل يجمعها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r6.claim: As an inward reading of the light parable, the mosques are niches, men are glass, hearts are lamps, their prompting meanings are radiance, purified upright bodies are the tree, and their beautiful secrets are its oil.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r6.anchor: المصابيح هي القلوب , وتلألؤها ما تشتمل عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r7.claim: The author mentions a report that mosques are to heaven's people what stars are to earth's people, without giving its authority or a grading.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r7.anchor: وقد ورد في بعض الأخبار أن المساجد لأهل السماوات كالنجوم لأهل الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī's al-Awsaṭ reports from Ibn ʿUmar an inward gloss: the niche is Muḥammad's interior, the glass his heart, the lamp its light, Abraham the tree, and neither east nor west means neither Jew nor Christian. No grading is given.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r8.anchor: وفي معجم الطبراني في الأوسط عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : ( كمسكاة ) قال : جوف محمد

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies these houses as mosques, honored and free from idle talk. God's name is recalled by Qur'an recitation, tasbih means prayer, and dawn/evening mean Fajr and Asr, the first prescribed prayers God loves to mention.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: هي المساجد تكرم ونهى عن اللغو فيها

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.claim: The Prophet says that at the gathering on Judgment Day a herald will call for the generous, those who left their beds for worship, those not distracted by trade, and those who praised God.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يجمع الناس في صعيد واحد ينفذهم البصر ويسمعهم الداعي

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r6.claim: Qatada identifies the houses as mosques and says God authorized their construction and elevation and commanded their maintenance and purification.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: هي المساجد أذن الله في بنيانها

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r7.claim: Mujahid says the houses are mosques authorized to be built.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: في مساجد أن تبنى

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says “raised” means exalted through God's remembrance and that glorifying Him there means praying.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r8.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {أذن الله أن ترفع} يقول: أن تعظم بذكره {يسبح} يصلي

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r9.claim: Mujahid offers a different referent: the houses are the houses of the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: هي بيوت النبي

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the houses to four mosques built by prophets: the Kaaba, Jerusalem, the Prophet's mosque, and Quba.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r10.anchor: عن ابن زيد {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: إنما هي أربع مساجد لم يبنهن إلا نبي

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r1.claim: After the Prophet said the houses were those of prophets, Abu Bakr asked whether Ali and Fatima's home was among them; the Prophet answered yes, one of their finest. The report is transmitted from Anas and Burayda.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r1.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك وبريدة قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r2.claim: When a man called in the mosque for a red camel, the Prophet told him three times that he would not find it and said mosques were built for their intended purpose.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r2.anchor: عن ابن بريدة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع رجلا يقول: من دعا إلى الجمل الأحمر

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r3.speaker: أبو سنان الشيباني
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r3.anchor: قال أبو سنان الشيباني في قوله {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: تعظم

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r4.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet ordered mosques to be built in neighborhoods and to be cleaned and perfumed.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r4.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ببناء المساجد في الدور

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r5.claim: Urwa transmits from an unnamed Companion that the Prophet directed people to establish mosques in their homes, improve their construction, and purify them.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r5.anchor: عن عروة بن الزبير عمن حدثه من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا: كان رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r6.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that Umar perfumed the mosque every Friday.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن عمر كان يجمر المسجد في كل جمعة

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r7.claim: Anas reports that spitting in a mosque is a sin and covering it is its expiation.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التفل في المسجد خطيئة وكفارته

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r8.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r8.claim: Abu Umama reports that spitting in a mosque is a sin and burying it is a good deed.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r8.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم البزاق في المسجد خطيئة ودفنه حسنة

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r9.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that spitting in a mosque is a sin and burying it is its expiation.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم البزاق في المسجد خطيئة وكفارته دفنه

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r10.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r10.claim: Ibn Umar reports that spitting in a mosque is a sin and burying it is its expiation.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r10.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم البزاق في المسجد خطيئة وكفارته دفنه

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r11.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r11.claim: Ibn Umar reports that phlegm directed toward the prayer niche will be raised on Judgment Day in the face of the person who spat.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r11.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تبعث النخامة يوم القيامة في القبلة

DURR-FULL:v6p203/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r12.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r12.claim: The Prophet says that whoever spits toward the qibla without covering it will meet it on Judgment Day, hot, between the eyes.
DURR-FULL:v6p203/r12.anchor: عن أبي أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من بزق في قبلة ولم يوارها جاءت يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r1.claim: Thawban reports that a person reciting poetry in a mosque should be told three times “May God destroy your mouth”; one seeking lost property should be told three times “May you not find it”; traders should be told their trade will not profit.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r1.anchor: عن ثوبان قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من رأيتموه ينشد شعرا في المسجد

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r2.claim: Jubayr ibn Mut'im reports prohibitions on unsheathing swords, scattering arrowheads, swearing, and denying a resident or guest a midday rest in mosques; images and glass ornamentation are also forbidden, since mosques are built in trust and honored.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r2.anchor: عن جبير بن مطعم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لاتسل السيوف ولا تنثر النبل

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r3.claim: Jubayr ibn Mut'im reports the Prophet's prohibition on carrying out prescribed punishments in mosques.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r3.anchor: عن جبير بن مطعم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تقام الحدود في المساجد

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas told a man who removed a pebble from the mosque to return it or face his complaint on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال لرجل أخرج حصاة من المسجد: ردها وإلا خاصمتك يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r5.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r5.claim: Ka'b says a pebble removed from a mosque pleads against its owner.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r5.anchor: عن كعب قال: إن الحصاة إذا أخرجت من المسجد تناشد صاحبها

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r6.claim: Mujahid says a pebble taken from the mosque cries out or glorifies God.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: إذا خرجت الحصاة من المسجد صاحت أو سبحت

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says a pebble curses whoever removes it from the mosque.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: الحصاة تسب وتلعن من يخرجها من المسجد

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r8.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r8.claim: Sulayman ibn Yasar says a pebble cries until it is returned to its place in the mosque.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r8.anchor: عن سليمان بن يسار قال: الحصاة إذا خرجت من المسجد تصيح حتى ترد إلى موضعها

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r9.speaker: فاطمة بنت رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r9.claim: Fatima reports that the Prophet's mosque-entry supplication asks forgiveness and the doors of mercy, while the exit version asks forgiveness and the doors of God's bounty.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r9.anchor: عن فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل المسجد يقول:

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r10.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r10.claim: Qatada reports the Prophet's instruction to give mosques their due; that due is two rakʿas before sitting.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r10.anchor: عن قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: اعطوا المساجد حقها قيل: وما حقها

DURR-FULL:v6p205/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿud says one sign of the Hour is that mosques become thoroughfares.
DURR-FULL:v6p205/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: من أشراط الساعة أن تتخذ المساجد طرقا

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r1.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r1.claim: Asim is reported to have read yusabbiḥ with the bāʾ in the accusative form (fatḥa).
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r1.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ (يسبح) بنصب الباء

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an contains the Duha prayer, though only the deeply searching notice it, citing this verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن صلاة الضحى لفي القرآن وما يغوص عليها الأغواص

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the houses as mosques, to be honored, where idle talk is forbidden; the same view is reported from ʿIkrima, Abū Ṣāliḥ, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, Abū Bakr ibn Sulaymān ibn Abī Khaythama, and Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة ، عن ابن عباس قوله : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع وهي المساجد يكرمونهن ونهى عن اللغو فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r2.speaker: ابن بريدة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r2.claim: Ibn Burayda says these are four mosques built only by prophets; he names the Kaaba (built by Abraham and Ishmael), Bayt Ariha/Jerusalem (built by David and Solomon), and the Prophet’s mosque in Medina.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r2.anchor: عن ابن بريدة يعني قوله : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع قال : انما هي اربع مساجد لم يبنهن الا نبي

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the houses as the homes of the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه قال : هي بيوت النبي

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says the phrase refers to all houses.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع قال : البيوت كلها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r5.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the houses as residences where people live and remember God, distinguishing them from the mosques God named.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع قال : هي المساكن . المسكن يعمرونه ويذكرون الله فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r6.speaker: سفيان بن الحسين
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r6.claim: Sufyān ibn al-Ḥusayn identifies the houses as mosques.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r6.anchor: عن سفيان بن الحسين : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع قال : هي المساجد

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies them as Jerusalem, because ten thousand lamps are lit there every night.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن هو بيت المقدس ؛ لانه يسرج فيه كل ليلة عشرة الاف قنديل

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r8.claim: Mujāhid says these are mosques that are built.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2604/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع قال : مساجد تبنى

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا سنان عن ثابت عن الضحاك في قوله : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع قال : تعظم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the houses as mosques whose construction and elevation God authorized, and whose maintenance and purification He commanded.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه وهي هذه المساجد ، اذن الله في بنائها ورفعها ، وامر بعمارتها وتطهيرها

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r3.speaker: كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r3.claim: Kaʿb says the Torah calls mosques God’s houses and promises honor to the person who performs ablution well and visits one, since a visitor is owed hospitality.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر لنا ان كعبا كان يقول : ان في التوراة مكتوبا : ' الا ان بيوتي في الارض المساجد

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains remembering God’s name there as reciting His Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ويذكر فيها اسمه يقول : يتلى فيها كتابه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r5.speaker: أبو روق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r5.claim: Abū Rawq interprets remembering God’s name there as prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r5.anchor: عن أبي روق ويذكر فيها اسمه يعني الصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains their glorification as performing prayer there in the morning and evening.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس يسبح له فيها يقول يصلي له فيها بالغدو والاصال

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
