IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r7.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān likewise says that they pray to God there at morning and evening.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل ابن حيان قوله : يسبح له فيها بالغدو والاصال يقول : يصلي لله فيها بالغداة والعشي

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies «morning» as the dawn prayer; Muqātil is also reported to say the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : بالغداة صلاة الغداة ، وروى عن مقاتل نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the evening prayers as the ʿAṣr prayer; he says these were the first two prayers made obligatory, singled out to be remembered and to remind God’s servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r9.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس قوله : والاصال يعني بالاصال صلاة العصر ، وهما اول ما فرض الله من الصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r10.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r10.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān glosses al-āṣāl as evening; the same is reported from al-Layth ibn Saʿd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2605/r10.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : يسبح له فيها بالغدو والاصال قال : الاصال العشي

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2606/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2606/r1.speaker: أبو روق
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2606/r1.claim: Abū Rawq identifies the morning time as the dawn prayer and the evening time as the period when the sun declines toward the sunset prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2606/r1.anchor: عن أبي روق : يسبح له فيها بالغدو والاصال يعني صلاة الغداة والاصال حين تميل الشمس إلى صلاة المغرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r1.claim: Exegetes debate how “in houses” connects to the preceding lamp parable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r1.anchor: تردد المفسرون في تعلق الجار والمجرور من قوله : { في بيوت } الخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r2.claim: One parsing attaches “in houses” to “is lit,” locating the lamp in houses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r2.anchor: فقيل يتعلق بقوله : { يوقد } ( النور : 35 ) أي يوقد المصباح في بيوت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r3.claim: Another parsing makes the phrase an adjective of “niche”; singular niche and lamp can pair with plural houses because each noun denotes a generic class.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r4.claim: The view that the houses are Muslim mosques does not work for the revelation period: Muslim mosques then had no lamps; mosque lamps appeared under ʿUmar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r4.anchor: ولا يستقيم ذلك إذ لم يكن في مساجد المسلمين يومئذ مصابيح وإنما أحدثت المصابيح في المساجد الإسلامية في خلافة عمر بن الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r5.claim: A report says Tamīm al-Dārī lit the Prophet's mosque with lamps brought from Syria, but he converted only in year nine, after the verse's revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r5.anchor: وروي أن تميما الداري أسرج المسجد النبوي بمصابيح جاء بها من الشام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r6.claim: Some identify the houses as Jerusalem churches that were then Christian churches.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r6.anchor: وقيل البيوت مساجد بيت المقدس وكانت يومئذ بيعا للنصارى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr proposes monks' cells and monasteries, familiar to Arabs along the Syrian route and used to host travelers; their elevated construction suits the wording about being raised.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز عندي على هذا الوجه أن يكون المراد بالبيوت صوامع الرهبان وأديرتهم وكانت معروفة في بلاد العرب في طريق الشام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r8.claim: God's permission means inspiring their builders to raise the houses; the monks were righteous and read the Gospel, and the cell and monastery on mountain heights fit this sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r8.anchor: والمراد بإذن الله برفعها أنه ألهم متخذيها أن يجعلوها عالية وكانوا صالحين يقرأون الإنجيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r9.claim: God did not command monastic dwellings in original Christianity, but did not forbid them; their permitted construction, joined with an intention to aid worship, became pleasing to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r9.anchor: لأن الله لم يأمرهم باتخاذ الأديرة في أصل النصرانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says Christian scholars' effort and divine inspiration supplied them with signs of religious legislation, as Gospel texts suggest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r10.anchor: وقد كان اجتهاد أحبار الدين في النصرانية وإلهامهم دلائل تشريع لهم كما تقتضيه نصوص من الإنجيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r11.claim: The vivid houses make the compared image clearer and more attractive, as in the Prophet's image of Hell's hooks like the saʿdān thorn and in Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr's poem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p244#2/r11.anchor: والمقصد من ذكر هذا على هذه الوجوه زيادة إيضاح المشبه به كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صفة جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r1.speaker: كعب بن زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r1.claim: The cited Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr couplet beautifies the image through descriptions of the house and its surroundings, making it more appealing to believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r1.anchor: شجت بذي شبم من ماء محنية صافف بأبطح أضحى وهو مشمول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r2.claim: On the monastery reading, the text specifies men because monks were men.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r2.anchor: وتخصيص التسبيح بالرجال لأن الرهبان كانوا رجالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites Imruʾ al-Qays's image of a monk's beacon shining at dusk as evidence that Arabs knew the lit cells.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r5.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس : تضيء الظلام بالعشي كأنها منارة ممسى راهب متبتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r6.claim: In Imruʾ al-Qays's second cited line, al-salīṭ means oil poured on lamp wicks, making their light stronger.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r7.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r7.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays likens stars to lamps in monks' cells, which guided people traveling at night; qaffāl means travelers returning from journeys.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r7.anchor: سموت إليها والنجوم كأنها مصابيح رهبان تشب لقفال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r8.claim: An alternative takes raising the houses in a spiritual sense, as exaltation and purification; on this view God's permission means a command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r8.anchor: وقيل : أريد بالرفع الرفع المعنوي وهو التعظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r9.claim: He rejects spiritual elevation as remote from the Qur'an's aims, especially in a Medinan passage that lavishly praises the men and promises their reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r9.anchor: وبعد فهذا يبعد عن أغراض القرآن وخاصة المدني منه لأن الثناء على هؤلاء الرجال ثناء جم ومعقب بقوله : { ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما عملوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r10.claim: His preferred parsing makes “in houses” a settled circumstantial phrase modifying “His light” in 24:35; this shows that the light means the Qur'an and portrays Muslims receiving, reciting, and studying it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r10.anchor: والأظهر عندي : أن قوله : { في بيوت } ظرف مستقر هو حال من { نوره }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r11.claim: The Prophet says that people gathering in a house of God to recite and study scripture receive tranquility and mercy, are surrounded by angels, and are remembered by God among those near Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r11.anchor: وما اجتمع قوم في بيت من بيوت الله يتلون كتاب الله ويتدارسونه بينهم إلا نزلت عليهم السكينة وغشيتهم الرحمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r1.claim: The Qur'anic verse surpasses Ṭarafa's verse because it combines tajrīd with explicit explanation of the image, while the poem uses tajrīd alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r1.anchor: وفي الحي أحوى ينفض المرد شادف مظاهر سمطي لؤلؤ وزبرجد مع ما في الآية من بيان ما أجمل في لفظ : { مثل نوره }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r2.claim: Alternatively, “in houses” begins a fresh clause and attaches to “glorifies Him therein”; fronting emphasizes the houses and builds anticipation, while “therein” repeats them for emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { في بيوت } غير مرتبط بما قبله وأنه مبدأ استئناف ابتدائي وأن المجرور متعلق بقوله : { يسبح له فيها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r3.claim: The Prophet says congregational prayer in the mosque is worth twenty-seven degrees more than prayer at home.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r3.anchor: صلاة أحدكم في المسجد ( أي الجماعة ) تفضل صلاته في بيته بسبع وعشرين درجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.claim: Another possible parse makes “in houses” the fronted predicate and “men” the subject, answering the implied question of who is guided to God's light in 24:35.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يكون { في بيوت } خبرا مقدما و { رجال } مبتدأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r6.claim: Al-ghudūw is morning, when people set out to attend to their affairs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r6.anchor: والمراد بالغدو : وقت الغدو وهو الصباح لأنه وقت خروج الناس في قضاء شؤونهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r7.claim: Al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the late afternoon; Ibn ʿĀshūr also refers to 7:205 and 13:15.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r7.anchor: والآصال : جمع أصيل وهو آخر النهار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r2.claim: The majority read yusabbiḥu with kasrah as active, making “men” its subject; Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥah as passive, making one of its three prepositional phrases the deputy subject and “men” the subject of an implied verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { يسبح } بكسر الموحدة بالبناء للفاعل و { رجال } فاعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.claim: For the passive reading, the “men” clause is resumed with an omitted verb prompted by yusabbiḥu, as in Nahshal ibn Ḥarrī's verse about a mourner weeping for Yazīd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.anchor: على نحو قول نهشل بن حري يرثي أخاه يزيد

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r1.claim: The absolute Light’s inward reality is, at the fullest realization, self-evident; none knows God except God.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r1.anchor: النور المطلق والمدلول باطنه وفي التحقيق الأتم هو دليل على نفسه لا يعرف الله إلا الله سبحانه

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r2.claim: “In houses” syntactically attaches to the later verb “is glorified.”
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r2.anchor: متعلق بالفعل المذكور بعده وهو يسبح

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r3.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r3.claim: Al-Raghib says bayt first meant a human’s night dwelling, then any dwelling; buyut usually means houses, abyat poetry, and the term also extends to a place where something is located.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r3.anchor: المفردات" : أصل البيت مأوى الإنسان بالليل ثم قد يقال من غير اعتبار الليل

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the houses as all mosques, God’s houses on earth that shine for heaven’s inhabitants as stars shine on earth.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r4.anchor: والمراد بالبيوت المساجد كلها لقول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض تضيء لأهل السماء

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r5.claim: Permission means informing someone that a thing is allowed and granting leave for it.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r5.anchor: الإذن في الشيء إعلام بإجازته والرخصة فيه

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r6.claim: The mosques are to be raised by construction, reverence, and elevated rank.

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r7.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes raising physical objects, buildings, renown, and status, illustrating each sense with Qur’anic verses.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r7.anchor: الإمام الراغب : الرفع يقال تارة في الأجسام الموضوعة إذا أعليتها عن مقرها

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r8.claim: God’s name may denote His essence or an attribute of negation, affirmation, or action; it is general for every kind of remembrance, including tawhid, Qur’an, religious study, call to prayer, and its commencement.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r8.anchor: اسم الله تعالى ما يصح أن يطلق عليه بالنظر إلى ذاته أو باعتبار صفة من صفاته السلبية كالقدوس أو الثبوتية كالعليم

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r9.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r9.claim: Some scholars hold that divine names are restricted to names established by transmitted authority.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r9.anchor: لكنها توقيفية عند بعض العلماء وهو عام في كل ذكر توحيدا كان أو تلاوة قرآن

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r10.claim: The Persian gloss urges worshippers to occupy mosques with remembrance and prayer and avoid worldly or idle talk; an attributed report says mosque talk consumes good deeds like grazing animals consume grass.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r10.anchor: وفي الأثر : "الحديث في المسجد يأكل الحسنات كما تأكل البهيمة الحشيش

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r11.claim: Repeating “in them” emphasizes and recalls the preceding phrase across the intervening words; fronting it signals importance, not that glorification is confined to mosques.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r11.anchor: فيها تكرير لقوله في بيوت للتأكيد والتذكير لما بينهما من الفاصلة

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r12.claim: Tasbih is declaring God’s transcendence; the word evokes swift movement through worship and extends to worship by speech, deed, or intention, here meaning the obligatory prayers.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r12.anchor: والتسبيح تنزيه الله وأصله المر السريع في عبادة الله فإن السبح المر السريع في الماء أو في الهواء

BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r13.claim: The specified times indicate obligatory prayers: ghuduww means the dawn prayer, while asal gathers the remaining prayers, as al-Kawashi explains.
BURSEVI:v6p114#3/r13.anchor: فالمراد بالغدو وقت صلاة الفجر المؤداة بالغداة وبالآصال ما عداه من أوقات صلوات الظهر والعصر والعشاءين

BURSEVI:v6p115/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115/r1.claim: Ghuduww is a verbal noun for entering morning time, between dawn prayer and sunrise; paired with asal, it is applied to the time itself.
BURSEVI:v6p115/r1.anchor: الغدو مصدر يقال : غدا يغدو غدوا أي دخل في وقت الغدوة وهي ما بين صلاة الغداة وطلوع الشمس

BURSEVI:v6p115/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115/r2.claim: Asal is the plural of asil, the evening period extending from the sun’s decline until dawn.
BURSEVI:v6p115/r2.anchor: جمع أصيل وهو العشي أي من زوال الشمس إلى طلوع الفجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r1.claim: Sura names date from the revelation period and make reference and review easier; a report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet directed each revealed verse to its sura.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r1.anchor: وقد دل حديث ابن عباس الذي ذكر آنفا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول إذا نزلت الآية وضعوها في السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r2.claim: The purpose of a sura name is to distinguish that sura from the others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r2.anchor: وفائدة التسمية أن تكون بما يميز السورة عن غيرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r3.claim: Names may have developed from ‘the sura in which X is mentioned’ by dropping the relative clause and then the implied noun, or may directly affiliate the sura with a related subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r3.anchor: وأصل أسماء السور أن تكون بالوصف كقولهم السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا ، ثم شاع فحذفوا الموصول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r4.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits from Aisha an account associated with the revelation of the final verses of al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r4.anchor: وقد ثبت في صحيح البخاري قول عائشة رضي الله عنها لما نزلت الآيات من آخر البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r5.claim: A report in al-Bukhari says the Prophet recited al-Najm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r5.anchor: وفيه عن ابن مسعود قال قرأ رسول الله النجم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet prostrated during al-Najm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن رسول الله سجد بالنجم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r7.speaker: أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r7.claim: A marfu‘ report attributed to Anas prohibits saying names such as Surat al-Baqara, Surat Aal Imran, or Surat al-Nisa, and directs people to say ‘the sura in which’.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r7.anchor: وما روى من حديث عن أنس مرفوعا لا تقولوا سورة البقرة ولا سورة آل عمران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r8.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r8.claim: Ahmad ibn Hanbal grades the prohibition report as munkar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r8.anchor: فقال أحمد بن حنبل هو حديث منكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r9.speaker: ابن الجوزي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r9.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi includes the Anas report in his collection of fabricated reports.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r10.speaker: ابن حجر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r10.claim: Ibn Hajar, by contrast, authenticates the report.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r11.claim: Ibn Umar is said to have used the same wording without attributing it to the Prophet; al-Bayhaqi records it in Shu‘ab al-Iman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r11.anchor: ويذكر عن ابن عمر أنه كان يقول مثل ذلك ولا يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r12.speaker: الحجاج بن يوسف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r12.claim: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf also forbade people to say ‘sura of X’ and ordered the longer descriptive form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r12.anchor: وكان الحجاج بن يوسف يمنع من يقول سورة كذا ويقول قل السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r13.speaker: الذين صححوا حديث أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r13.claim: Those who authenticated the prohibition explain it as a Meccan response to mockery when Muslims used names such as al-Fil and al-Ankabut.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r13.anchor: والذين صححوا حديث أنس تأولوه وتأولوا قول ابن عمر بأن ذلك كان في مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r15.claim: The prohibition did not become established practice; al-Bukhari’s chapter heading says there is no harm in naming suras, and its reports give examples including some wording from the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r15.anchor: ولهذا ترجم البخاري في كتاب فضائل القرآن بقوله باب من لم ير بأسا أن يقول سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r16.claim: The author permits both the descriptive name and forms such as Surat al-Najm, citing the several designations in Ibn Abbas’s prostration report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r16.anchor: وعليه فللقائل أن يقول سورة البقرة أو التي يذكر فيها البقرة ، وأن يقول سورة والنجم وسورة النجم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r17.claim: The Companions apparently used names learned from the Prophet or familiar popular names; Ibn Masud’s naming of the two qunut suras al-Khal‘ and al-Hafd shows that some names were his own.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r17.anchor: والظاهر أن الصحابة سموا بما حفظوه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو أخذوا لها أشهر الأسماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r18.claim: Sura names can describe a quality, a distinctive subject, a person treated at length, or words occurring in the sura.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r18.anchor: واعلم أن أسماء السور إما أن تكون بأوصافها مثل الفاتحة وسورة الحمد ، وإما أن تكون بالإضافة لشيء اختصت بذكره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r19.claim: The suras beginning with Ha Mim are collectively called Al-Hawamim; al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas share the descriptive name al-Muqashqishatan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r19.anchor: وقد سموا مجموع السور المفتتحة بكلمة حم آل حم وربما سموا السورتين بوصف واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r20.claim: The Companions omitted sura titles from the codex to avoid inserting non-Quranic text, using the basmala to mark divisions because it suits openings and is itself Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r20.anchor: واعلم أن الصحابة لم يثبتوا في المصحف أسماء السور بل اكتفوا بإثبات البسملة في مبدأ كل سورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r21.claim: Al-Itqan says al-Bayyina was called Surat Ahl al-Kitab in Ubayy’s codex, suggesting he did write sura names there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r21.anchor: وفي الإتقان أن سورة البينة سميت في مصحف أبى سورة أهل الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r22.claim: Sura names were regularly written in codices during the Followers’ period without objection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r22.anchor: وكتبت أسماء السور في المصاحف باطراد في عصر التابعين ولم ينكر عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r23.speaker: المازري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p90/r23.claim: Al-Maziri quotes al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani: sura titles were written in a different script to distinguish them from Quran, while the basmala matched Quranic script.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r1.claim: The preposition in “fī buyūtin” may be read with either ḍamma or kasra on the bāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥātim says “fī” attaches to “miṣbāḥ” in 24:35, while another view attaches it to the later “yusabbiḥu,” requiring a pause at “ʿalīm” in 24:38.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم وقيل متعلقة ب يسبح المتأخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r3.speaker: الرماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r3.anchor: قال الرماني هي متعلقة ب يوقد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid identify the houses as mosques devoted to God and customarily lit with such lamps.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد هي المساجد المخصوصة لله تعالى التي من عادتها أن تنور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r5.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan identifies the houses as the chambers of Bayt al-Maqdis, called houses because its sections are separated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن أراد بيت المقدس وسماه بيوتا من حيث فيه مواضيع يتحيز بعضها عن بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya recounts that Israelites meticulously lit Bayt al-Maqdis with selected, sealed, specially prepared and consecrated oil, making it the brightest house on earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r6.anchor: وكان الزيت منتخبا مختوما على ظروفه قد صنع صنعة وقدس حتى لا يجزى الوقيد بغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r7.claim: ʿIkrima takes the houses broadly as houses of faith, including mosques and homes where lamps were lit for night prayer and study.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة أراد بيوت الإيمان على الإطلاق مساجد ومساكن فهي التي يستصبح فيها بالليل للصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid also identifies the houses as the houses of the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد أراد بيوت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.claim: The following description of men glorifying God in the houses supports identifying them as mosques.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال يقوي أنها المساجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r10.claim: “Adhina” means commanded or decreed; permission literally means knowledge and enablement without prohibition, strengthened when accompanied by command and execution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r10.anchor: أذن بمعنى أمر وقضى، وحقيقة الإذن العلم والتمكين دون حظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r1.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r1.claim: Mujāhid and others explain “raised” as built and elevated, as with Abraham raising the foundations in 2:127.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r1.anchor: ترفع، قيل معناه تبنى وتعلى، قاله مجاهد وغيره فذلك كنحو قوله تعالى: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r2.claim: The Prophet said whoever builds a mosque from his own property will have a house built for him in Paradise; Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes related hadiths.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r2.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «من بنى مسجدا من ماله بنى الله له بيتا في الجنة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r3.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan and others explain “raised” as honored and elevated in standing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن وغيره معناه تعظم ويرفع شأنها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r4.claim: Mentioning God's name in the houses means prayer and worship through speech and action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r4.anchor: وذكر اسمه تعالى، هو بالصلاة والعبادة قولا وفعلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r5.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read “yusabbiḥu” with fatḥa on the doubled bāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم «يسبح» بفتح الباء المشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r6.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r6.claim: The other readers and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read “yusabbiḥu” with kasra on the doubled bāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وحفص عن عاصم «يسبح» بكسر الباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.claim: With the first reading, “rijāl” is subject of an implied verb indicated by “yusabbiḥu”; Sibawayh compares the construction to a poetic line meaning “a suppliant weeps for him.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.anchor: ف رجال على القراءة الأولى مرتفع بفعل مضمر يدل عليه يسبح تقديره يسبحه رجال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.claim: With the second reading, “rijāl” is the subject of the explicit verb “yusabbiḥu.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.anchor: ورجال على القراءة الثانية مرتفع ب يسبح الظاهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r9.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads the verb with tāʾ instead of yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r9.anchor: وروي عن يحيى بن وثاب أنه قرأ «تسبح» بالتاء من فوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r10.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says “al-ghuduww wa-al-āṣāl” means morning and noon.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the phrase as the two rakʿas of ḍuḥā and the ʿaṣr prayer, adding that ḍuḥā is in God's Book for those who can discern it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أراد ركعتي الضحى والعصر وإن ركعتي الضحى لفي كتاب الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj connects fī to the niche phrase, yielding a niche in houses; alternatively it connects to glorification, with fīhā repeated for emphasis and men glorifying God in houses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج في من صلة قوله كمشكاة فالمعنى كمشاكة في بيوت ويجوز أن تكون متصلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r2.claim: The singular niche with plural houses is explained either by a shift from singular to plural address, as at 33:1, or by each house having its own niche.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r2.anchor: أنه من الخطاب المتلون الذي يفتح بالتوحيد ويختم بالجمع كقوله يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r3.claim: The houses are the mosques, according to Ibn Abbas and most commentators.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r3.anchor: أحدهما انها المساجد قاله ابن عباس والجمهور والثاني بيوت أزواج رسول الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the houses as the homes of the Prophet's wives.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r4.anchor: والثاني بيوت أزواج رسول الله ( ص ) قاله مجاهد والثالث بيت المقدس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r5.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the houses as the Jerusalem sanctuary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r5.anchor: قاله مجاهد والثالث بيت المقدس قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r6.claim: Aḏina means that God commanded it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r6.anchor: فأما أذن فمعنا امر وفي معنى ان ترفع قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r7.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r7.claim: Hasan and al-Dahhak take raising the houses to mean honoring them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r7.anchor: أحدها أن تعظم قاله الحسن والضحاك والثاني أن تبنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r8.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r8.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take raising the houses to mean building them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r8.anchor: قاله الحسن والضحاك والثاني أن تبنى قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r9.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas explains mentioning God's name as affirming His oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r9.anchor: أحدهما توحيده رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس والثاني يتلى فيها كتابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r10.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas explains it as reciting God's Book in the houses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r10.anchor: والثاني يتلى فيها كتابه رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r11.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r11.claim: These readers pronounce yusabbiḥu with kasra on bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r11.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي يسبح بكسر الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r12.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r12.claim: They pronounce yusabbiḥu with fatḥa on bāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r12.anchor: وقرأ بن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم بفتحها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r13.speaker: معاذ القارئ وأبو حيوة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r13.claim: They read tusabbaḥu with a feminine tāʾ, kasra on bāʾ, and a nominative ending on ḥāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r13.anchor: وقرأ معاذ القارئ وأبو حيوة تسبح بتاء مرفوعة وكسر الباء ورفع الحاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r14.claim: One interpretation takes the glorification as prayer; the other takes it as the familiar verbal tasbīḥ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r14.anchor: وفي قوله يسبح له فيها قولان أحدهما أنه الصلاة ثم في صلاة الغدو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r15.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas identifies the morning prayer as Fajr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r15.anchor: أحدهما أنها صلاة الفجر رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس والثاني صلاة الضحى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Duha prayer is found in God's Book and cites this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r16.anchor: روى ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس قال إن صلاة الضحى لفي كتاب الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r17.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r17.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says the afternoon prayers are noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r17.anchor: أحدهما أنها صلاة الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r18.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r18.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi identifies the afternoon prayer as ʿAsr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r18.anchor: والثاني صلاة العصر قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي والقول الثاني أنه التسبيح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r19.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r19.claim: A second interpretation takes the words as ordinary glorification of God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p45/r19.anchor: والقول الثاني أنه التسبيح المعروف ذكره بعض المفسرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r1.claim: After likening the believer's heart, guidance, and knowledge to a lamp in clear glass fueled by good oil, Ibn Kathir identifies its setting as mosques, God's beloved houses for worship and oneness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r1.anchor: قلب المؤمن، وما فيه من الهدى والعلم، بالمصباح في الزجاجة الصافية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r2.claim: God commands mosques to be elevated by cleansing them of filth, idle talk, and unsuitable actions and speech.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r2.anchor: أي: بتطهيرها من الدنس واللغو، والأفعال والأقوال التي لا تليق فيها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the command to raise mosques as a prohibition on idle talk in them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r3.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية الكريمة: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} قال: نهى الله سبحانه عن اللغو فيها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r4.speaker: عكرمة، وأبو صالح، والضحاك، ونافع بن جبير، وأبو بكر بن سليمان بن أبي حثمة، وسفيان بن حسين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r4.claim: These named exegetes are also cited for interpreting the verse as forbidding idle talk in mosques.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r4.anchor: وكذا قال عكرمة، وأبو صالح، والضحاك، ونافع بن جبير، وأبو بكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r5.claim: Qatada identifies the houses as mosques that God ordered people to build, maintain, and purify.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: هي هذه المساجد، أمر الله، سبحانه، ببنائها ورفعها، وأمر بعمارتها وتطهيرها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r6.speaker: كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r6.claim: Kaab says the Torah calls mosques God's houses on earth and promises honor to one who visits after performing ablution well.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر لنا أن كعبا كان يقول: إن في التوراة مكتوبا: " ألا إن بيوتي في الأرض المساجد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r7.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r7.claim: Uthman reports the Prophet promising that whoever builds a mosque seeking God's face will receive its like in Paradise; the report is in both Sahih collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r7.anchor: فعن أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "من بنى مسجدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r8.claim: Ibn Majah transmits Umar's report from the Prophet that whoever builds a mosque for God's remembrance will have a house built for him in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r8.anchor: وروى ابن ماجه، عن عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r9.speaker: عمرو بن عبسة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r9.claim: Al-Nasai transmits from Amr ibn Abasa the same promise of a house in Paradise for building a mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62/r9.anchor: وللنسائي عن عمرو بن عبسة (7) مثله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet ordered mosques in residential areas to be built, cleaned, and perfumed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r1.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ببناء المساجد في الدور، وأن تنظف وتطيب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.claim: Ahmad and Abu Dawud transmit a similar report from Samura ibn Jundub about mosques in residential areas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r2.anchor: ولأحمد وأبي داود، عن سمرة بن جندب نحوه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Umar's instruction to provide people shelter while avoiding red or yellow mosque decoration that might distract them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r3.anchor: وقال البخاري: قال عمر: ابن للناس ما يكنهم، وإياك أن تحمر أو تصفر فتفتن الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.claim: Ibn Majah reports the Prophet saying that when a people act badly, they adorn their mosques; Ibn Kathir notes the chain is weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r4.anchor: وروى ابن ماجه عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما ساء عمل قوم قط إلا زخرفوا مساجدهم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.claim: In a report from Ibn Abbas, the Prophet says he was not commanded to embellish mosques.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r5.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما أمرت بتشييد المساجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas warns that Muslims will ornament mosques as Jews and Christians ornamented theirs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لتزخرفنها كما زخرفت اليهود والنصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying the Hour will not arrive until people boast competitively about their mosques.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r7.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تقوم الساعة حتى يتباهى الناس في المساجد"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.speaker: بريدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.claim: When a man called out in a mosque for his lost red camel, the Prophet prayed that he not find it and said mosques were built for their proper purpose.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r8.anchor: وعن بريدة أن رجلا أنشد في المسجد، فقال: من دعا إلى الجمل الأحمر؟ فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا وجدت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.claim: A report from Amr ibn Shuaib, his father, and grandfather says the Prophet prohibited trade and reciting poetry in mosques; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r9.anchor: وعن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، عن البيع والابتياع،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.claim: The Prophet instructs that a mosque trader be told God will not profit his trade, and someone seeking lost property be told God will not return it; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r10.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه سلم: قال: "إذا رأيتم من يبيع أو يبتاع في المسجد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.claim: A marfu report from Ibn Umar lists prohibited mosque uses: passage, displaying weapons, testing bows, scattering arrows, carrying raw meat, penalties, retaliation, and marketplaces.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r11.anchor: وقد روى ابن ماجه وغيره، من حديث ابن عمر مرفوعا، قال: "خصال لا تنبغي في المسجد: لا يتخذ طريقا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.claim: Wathila reports the Prophet's directions to keep children, the insane, trade, disputes, loud voices, penalties, and drawn swords from mosques, and to provide washing places and incense them on Fridays.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p62#2/r12.anchor: وعن واثلة بن الأسقع، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "جنبوا المساجد صبيانكم ومجانينكم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r1.claim: Ibn Majah also transmits the preceding directions about mosque conduct; Ibn Kathir says both chains are weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r1.anchor: ورواه ابن ماجه أيضا (1) وفي إسنادهما (2) ضعف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r2.claim: Some scholars dislike using a mosque as a thoroughfare unless necessary when another route is available; an athar says angels marvel at someone who passes through without praying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r2.anchor: كره بعض العلماء المرور فيه إلا لحاجة إذا وجد مندوحة عنه. وفي الأثر: "إن الملائكة لتتعجب من الرجل يمر بالمسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r3.claim: Weapons, bow practice, and scattered arrows are barred because they could injure the many worshippers; the Prophet instructed people carrying arrows to hold their heads so no one is hurt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r3.anchor: فلما يخشى من إصابة بعض الناس به، لكثرة المصلين فيه؛ ولهذا أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مر أحد بسهام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r4.claim: Raw meat should not be carried through because blood may drip; a menstruating woman should likewise avoid passing through if she fears soiling the mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r4.anchor: وأما النهي عن المرور باللحم النيء فيه، فلما يخشى من تقاطر الدم منه، كما نهيت الحائض عن المرور فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r5.claim: Penalties and retaliation are barred because the punished or injured person could leave impurity in the mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r5.anchor: فلما يخشى من إيجاد نجاسة فيه من المضروب أو المقطوع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r6.claim: A mosque is not a marketplace because trade is prohibited there; it was built for remembrance and prayer, as the Prophet told the Bedouin who urinated there before water was poured over it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r6.anchor: فلما تقدم من النهي عن البيع والشراء فيه، فإنه إنما بني لذكر الله والصلاة كما قال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says Umar would strike children playing in the mosque with a whip and patrol it after nightfall, allowing no one to remain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r7.anchor: وقد كان عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، إذا رأى صبيانا يلعبون في المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r8.claim: Children are kept away because their play is unsuitable; the mentally impaired because of weak judgment, mockery, play, or fear of soiling the mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r8.anchor: "ومجانينكم" يعني: لأجل ضعف عقولهم، وسخر الناس بهم، فيؤدي إلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r9.claim: Trade in mosques is barred, as already explained.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r10.speaker: كثير من العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r10.claim: Many scholars say judges should not hold court in mosques because cases bring disputes, arguments, and shouting that do not suit them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r10.anchor: نص كثير من العلماء على أن الحاكم لا ينتصب لفصل الأقضية في المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r11.claim: The prohibition on raising voices follows because the noise and clamor of disputes do not befit a mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64/r11.anchor: الذي لا يناسبه؛ ولهذا قال بعده: "ورفع أصواتكم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.speaker: السائب بن يزيد الكندي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.claim: Al-Saib ibn Yazid reports Umar summoning two men from Taif for raising their voices in the Prophet's mosque and saying he would have beaten them if they were locals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r1.anchor: عن السائب بن يزيد الكندي قال: كنت قائما في المسجد، فحصبني رجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf reports hearing Umar rebuke a man for raising his voice in the mosque; Ibn Kathir calls this report sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن إبراهيم، عن أبيه إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: سمع عمر صوت رجل في المسجد فقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r3.claim: The directions to keep penalties and drawn swords from mosques have already been discussed.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.claim: The washing places at mosque doors are facilities used for ablution and relieving oneself; wells near the Prophet's Mosque supplied water for drinking, washing, and ablution.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r4.anchor: يعني: المراحيض التي يستعان بها على الوضوء وقضاء الحاجة. وقد كانت قريبا من مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آبار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.claim: Incensing mosques on Fridays means perfuming them for the large Friday gathering.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r5.anchor: يعني: بخروها في أيام الجمع لكثرة اجتماع الناس يومئذ.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that Umar would incense the Prophet's Mosque every Friday; Ibn Kathir grades the chain hasan and acceptable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر؛ أن عمر كان يجمر مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كل جمعة. إسناده حسن لا بأس به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r1.speaker: الدارقطني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r1.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits a marfu report that a mosque's neighbor has no prayer except in the mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r1.anchor: وعند الدارقطني مرفوعا: "لا صلاة لجار المسجد إلا في المسجد"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r2.claim: A report in the Sunan gives glad tidings of complete light on Judgment Day to those who walk to mosques in darkness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r2.anchor: وفي السنن: "بشر المشائين إلى المساجد في الظلم بالنور التام يوم القيامة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r3.claim: It is recommended to enter the mosque with the right foot first.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r3.anchor: والمستحب لمن دخل المسجد أن يبدأ برجله اليمنى، وأن يقول كما ثبت في صحيح البخاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r4.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits from Abd Allah ibn Amr that the Prophet would seek refuge from Satan when entering the mosque; the narration says Satan declares the speaker protected for the rest of the day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو (11) رضي الله عنه (12) عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان إذا دخل المسجد قال: أعوذ بالله العظيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r5.speaker: أبو حميد أو أبو أسيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r5.claim: The Prophet instructs a mosque entrant to ask God to open the doors of mercy and, when leaving, to ask for His bounty; al-Nasai also transmits the same report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r5.anchor: روى مسلم بسنده عن أبي حميد -أو: أبي أسيد -قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد فليقل: اللهم افتح لي أبواب رحمتك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r6.claim: The Prophet instructs entrants and leavers to send blessings on him; entrants ask for mercy and leavers for protection from Satan. Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzayma, and Ibn Hibban transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r6.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد، فليسلم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وليقل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r7.speaker: فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r7.claim: Fatima reports the Prophet asking forgiveness and for mercy on entering, and forgiveness and bounty on leaving; al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan but disconnected because Fatima bint al-Husayn did not meet Fatima al-Kubra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p65/r7.anchor: عن جدتها فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r1.claim: All the cited material, along with further mosque reports omitted for length, falls under God's command concerning the houses where He is remembered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r1.anchor: فهذا الذي ذكرناه، مع ما تركناه من الأحاديث الواردة في ذلك لحال الطول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r2.claim: Remembering God's name in mosques is connected to commands to dress at every mosque, worship God sincerely there, and call on no one besides Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r2.anchor: وقوله: {ويذكر فيها اسمه} أي: اسم الله، كقوله: {يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembering God's name in mosques means reciting His Book there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {ويذكر فيها اسمه} يعني: يتلى فيها كتابه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r4.claim: Al-ghuduw refers to early mornings; al-asal is the plural of asil, meaning the end of the day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r4.anchor: وقوله: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال} أي: في البكرات والعشيات. والآصال: جمع أصيل، وهو آخر النهار.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports Ibn Abbas's view that every occurrence of tasbih in the Qur'an means prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: كل تسبيح في القرآن هو الصلاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the times as the dawn and afternoon prayers, the first prayers made obligatory, which God singled out to remember and remind His servants of.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r6.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: يعني بالغدو: صلاة الغداة، ويعني بالآصال: صلاة العصر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r7.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak likewise interpret glorifying God morning and evening as performing prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r7.anchor: وكذا قال الحسن، والضحاك: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال} يعني: الصلاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.claim: Some readers vocalize yusabbaḥu passively with fath on bāʾ; they pause fully at al-asal and restart with rijāl, which explains the omitted agent. The cited verse uses the same implicit-agent construction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ من القرأة (1) " يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال" -بفتح الباء من "يسبح" على أنه مبني لما لم يسم فاعله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.speaker: الشاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates an understood agent: a question asks who bewails Yazid, then the following phrase supplies the answer. This supports the passive reading's restart with rijāl.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.anchor: ليبك يزيد، ضارع لخصومة … ومختبط مما تطيح الطوائح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.claim: Readers with kasra on the bāʾ read an active verb whose subject is rijāl; the pause is therefore suitable only after that subject completes the clause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.anchor: وأما على قراءة من قرأ: {يسبح} -بكسر الباء -فجعله فعلا وفاعله: {رجال} فلا يحسن الوقف إلا على الفاعل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r1.claim: Women’s prayers are better in their homes; the reports further distinguish the innermost room as more meritorious than the house or chamber.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r1.anchor: فأما النساء فصلاتهن في بيوتهن أفضل لهن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r2.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Ibn Masud that a woman’s prayer at home is better than in her chamber, and in her private room better still.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "صلاة المرأة في بيتها أفضل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r3.claim: Ahmad reports Umm Salama’s narration that the best mosques for women are the innermost parts of their homes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r3.anchor: عن أم سلمة -رضي الله عنها، -عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "خير مساجد النساء [قعر] (5) بيوتهن"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r4.claim: Umm Humayd asked to pray with the Prophet; he ranked prayer progressively better from her home through the neighborhood mosque to his mosque. She built a dark mosque in the farthest part of her home and prayed there until death; Ibn Kathir says the report is not in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r4.anchor: أنها جاءت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: يا رسول الله، إني أحب الصلاة معك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r5.claim: A woman may attend the men’s congregational prayer if she does not harm men by displaying adornment or wearing perfume.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r5.anchor: ويجوز لها شهود جماعة الرجال، بشرط أن لا تؤذي أحدا من الرجال بظهور زينة ولا ريح طيب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r6.claim: Bukhari and Muslim report Ibn Umar’s narration that the Prophet said not to prevent God’s female servants from attending mosques.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تمنعوا إماء الله مساجد الله"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r7.speaker: أحمد وأبو داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r7.claim: Ahmad and Abu Dawud add that women’s homes are better for them; another wording says they should go out without perfume, which Ibn Kathir glosses as having no scent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r7.anchor: ولأحمد وأبي داود: "وبيوتهن خير لهن" (2) وفي رواية: "وليخرجن وهن تفلات" (3)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r8.claim: Muslim reports Zaynab, wife of Ibn Masud, saying the Prophet told women not to apply perfume if they attend the mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r8.anchor: عن زينب -امرأة ابن مسعود -قالت: قال لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا شهدت إحداكن المسجد فلا تمس طيبا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r9.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r9.claim: Aisha reports that believing women attended dawn prayer with the Prophet and returned wrapped in mantles, unrecognized in the darkness before dawn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p67/r9.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، أنها قالت: كان نساء المؤمنين (5) يشهدن الفجر مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r1.claim: Aisha says that had the Prophet seen what women introduced later, he would have barred them from mosques as Israelite women were barred; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r1.anchor: عنها أنها قالت: لو أدرك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أحدث النساء لمنعهن المساجد

JISHUMI:v7p5205/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5205/r6.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر عنه، وابن عامر، وقتادة، وأشهب العقيلي
JISHUMI:v7p5205/r6.claim: These authorities read يسبح passively and raise رجال as its passive subject; the pause is at الآصال.
JISHUMI:v7p5205/r6.anchor: قرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر عنه، وابن عامر، وقتادة، وأشهب العقيلي: يسبح بفتح الباء على ما لم يسم فاعله

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd connects في بيوت to the lamps, with the lamps’ implicit location serving as its syntactic governor.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r4.anchor: الأول: المصابيح في بيوت أذن الله، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r5.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj connects في بيوت to يسبح, as in saying Zayd stood in the house.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r5.anchor: والثاني: يتصل ب (يسبح)، كقولك: في الدار قام زيد فيها، عن الزجاج

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r6.claim: A third analysis connects في بيوت to توقد, meaning the lamps are lit in houses.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r6.anchor: والثالث: توقد في بيوت. وذكر أبو مسلم

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r7.claim: Abū Muslim connects في بيوت to the earlier mention of examples from those before, takes the houses as mosques, and understands those people as prophets; critics object that the earlier passage concerns deniers and is separated by intervening text.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r7.anchor: وذكر أبو مسلم وجها رابعا وهو أنه يتصل بقوله: (ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم) في بيوت، وهم الأنبياء

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r8.claim: Abū Muslim answers that the earlier phrase can refer to prophets and righteous people opposed by enemies, and that intervening material does not prevent a return to the earlier topic.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r8.anchor: والجواب لأبي مسلم: أنه يحتمل أنه أراد الأنبياء والصالحين الذين كادهم الأعداء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r1.claim: Fī buyūtin may attach to the preceding description: the niche lamp is in some of God’s houses, namely mosques.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r1.anchor: {فى بيوت } يتعلق بما قبله . أي : كمشكاة في بعض بيوت الله وهي المساجد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r2.claim: It may instead attach to yusabbiḥu, meaning men glorify God in houses; the repeated location is like saying someone is in the house sitting in it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r2.anchor: أو بما بعده ، وهو يسبح ، أي : يسبح له رجال في بيوت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r3.claim: A third parsing supplies an omitted verb, “glorify in houses,” as in the cited construction from 27:12.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r3.anchor: أو بمحذوف كقوله : { وأدخل يدك فى } ( النمل : 27 ) أي سبحوا في بيوت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r4.claim: God’s permission means His command, and raising the houses means building them, as in 79:28 and 2:127.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r4.anchor: والمراد بالإذن : الأمر . ورفعها : بناؤها ، كقوله :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are mosques that God commanded to be built.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي المساجد ، أمر الله أن تبنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also allows “raised” to mean that the mosques are honored and elevated in rank.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي المساجد ، أمر الله أن تبنى ، أو تعظيمها والرفع من قدرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r7.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command is not to raise the buildings but to honor them; the following mention of God’s name suits this reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله عنه : ما أمر الله أن ترفع بالبناء ، ولكن بالتعظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r8.claim: Mentioning God’s name in the houses applies generally to every kind of remembrance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r8.anchor: { ويذكر فيها اسمه } أوفق له ، وهو عام في كل ذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās specifies that God’s name is mentioned by reciting His Book there.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : وأن يتلى فيها كتابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r10.claim: Yusabbaḥu is also read passively and can attach to one of the adverbials; rijāl is nominative through the implied active yusabbiḥu.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r10.anchor: وقرىء : ( يسبح ) على البناء للمفعول ، ويسند إلى أحد الظروف الثلاثة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r11.claim: The reading tasabbaḥu has kasra on the bāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar reads tāʾ with fatḥa, making morning and evening times the subject, with their Lord intended.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r11.anchor: وتسبح ، بالتاء وكسر الباء . وعن أبي جعفر رضي الله عنه بالتاء وفتح الباء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r12.claim: Al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, meaning evening; bil-ghuduww means mornings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r12.anchor: والآصال : جمع أصل وهو العشي . والمعنى : بأوقات الغدو ، أي : بالغدوات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r13.claim: Another reading is wa-l-īṣāl, entering into evening; āṣala follows the patterns of aẓhara and aʿtama.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r13.anchor: قرىء : ( والإيصال ) وهو الدخول في الأصيل . يقال : آصل ، كأظهر وأعتم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Mujahid identify the houses as mosques.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنها المساجد , قاله ابن عباس , والحسن , ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r2.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r2.claim: Ikrima says the houses are all other houses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنها سائر البيوت , قاله عكرمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the houses being raised as their being built, as in Abraham raising the House's foundations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r3.anchor: أحدها : أن تبنى , قاله مجاهد كقوله : { وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت } أي يبني .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r4.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r4.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says the houses are raised by being cleansed of impurities and sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r4.anchor: الثاني : أنها تطهر من الأنجاس والمعاصي , حكاه ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r5.claim: Al-Hasan interprets raising the houses as honoring them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r6.claim: A fourth interpretation is that people's needs are raised to God in the houses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r6.anchor: الرابع : أن ترفع فيها الحوائج إلى الله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God's Book is recited in the houses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r7.anchor: أحدها : يتلى فيها كتابه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir says God's beautiful names are remembered there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r8.anchor: الثاني : تذكر فيها أسماؤه الحسنى , قاله ابن جرير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r9.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi says it means affirming God's oneness, that there is no deity besides Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r9.anchor: الثالث : توحيده بأن لا إله غيره , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r10.claim: “In houses” may attach backward to the niche containing a lamp in 24:35, or forward to “He is glorified in them.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r10.anchor: أحدهما : إلى ما تقدم من قوله : كمشكاة فيها مصباح

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r11.claim: The tasbih in the houses may mean declaring God transcendent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak interpret the tasbih as prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r12.anchor: في هذا التسبيح قولان : أحدهما : أنه تنزيه الله . الثاني : أنه الصلاة , قاله ابن عباس والضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r13.claim: Ghuduww is the plural of ghudwa, and asil's plural asāl means evening.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r13.anchor: الغدو جمع غدوة والآصال جمع أصيل وهي العشاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r30.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r30.claim: A report says that after this verse the Prophet ordered the Quba mosque built; ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha praised its builder and asked about those who pray standing and sitting and spend nights prostrating; the Prophet agreed, then told him to stop rhyming because nothing given to a servant is worse than a fluent tongue.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r30.anchor: وقيل لما نزلت هذه الآية أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ببناء مسجد قباء فحضر عبد الله بن رواحة

MUJAHID:v2p443/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p443/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p443/r1.claim: The houses God permitted to be raised are mosques built for worship.
MUJAHID:v2p443/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ﴾ قال مساجد تبنى

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r1.claim: God commanded the houses to be raised, meaning built and maintained.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r1.anchor: في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع } يقول: أمر الله، عز وجل، أن ترفع، يعني أن تبنى

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r2.claim: Mentioning God's name in them means declaring His oneness.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r2.anchor: ويذكر فيها اسمه } يعني يوحد الله عز وجل نظيرها في البقرة: { يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r3.claim: Their glorification of God morning and evening means that they pray to Him.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r3.anchor: يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال } [آية: 36] يقول: يصلي لله عز وجل.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r1.claim: “In houses” may attach to the niche in the preceding parable, meaning a niche in some mosques; repeating “in them” reinforces the wording.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r1.anchor: يتعلق بمشكاة أى كمشكاة فى بعض بيوت الله وهى المساجد كأنه قيل مثل نوره كما يرى فى المسجد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it attaches to an omitted command: “glorify in houses.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r2.anchor: أو بمحذوف أى سبحوا فى بيوت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r3.claim: God’s permission here means His command.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r4.claim: “Be raised” can mean built, as in verses about raising a structure and Abraham raising the foundations.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ أن ترفع ﴾ تبنى كقوله بناها رفع سمكها فسواها وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r5.claim: Hasan says God commanded that the houses be honored, not built.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن ما أمر الله أن نرفع بالبناء ولكن بالتعظيم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r6.claim: Remembering God’s name can mean reciting His Book or any form of remembrance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r6.anchor: ﴿ ويذكر فيها اسمه ﴾ يتلى فيها كتابه أو هو عام فى كل ذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.claim: Here “glorify” means pray: at dawn is the Fajr prayer, while the evening term includes Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ; dawn is singular because it has one prayer, while evening covers several.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال ﴾ أى يصلى له فيها بالغداة صلاة الفجر وبالآصال صلاة الظهر والعصر والعشاءين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the late afternoon.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.anchor: والآصال جمع أصل جمع أصيل وهو العشى

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r1.claim: The initial bāʾ in buyūt is read with either ḍamma or kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r1.anchor: الباء في «بيوت» تضم وتكسر وقد تقدم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r2.claim: Some attach “in houses” to “lamp” in the preceding light verse; others attach it to “he is glorified therein,” in which case one pauses at “Knowing.”

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reports Abu al-ʿAbbas’s view that the phrase is circumstantial for the lamp, glass, and star, as if saying that they are in houses.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: سمعت أبا العباس يقول هو حال للمصباح والزجاجة والكوكب كأنه قال وهي في بيوت

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r4.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم محمد بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Muhammad b. ʿAli treats “in houses” as a separate statement that God is in the houses; he cites a report that one who sits in a mosque is in the company of his Lord and a Torah report describing God’s welcome and Paradise as the believer’s hospitality when visiting the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r4.anchor: منفصل، كأنه يقول: الله في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says that attaching the phrase to “he is glorified therein,” or making it govern “men,” permits pausing at “God knows everything.”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r5.anchor: حسن الوقف على قوله «والله بكل شيء عليم»

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r6.speaker: الرماني
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r6.claim: Al-Rummani attaches the phrase to “is kindled,” which means there is no pause at “Knowing.”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r6.anchor: هي متعلقة ب«يوقد» وعليه فلا يوقف على «عليم»

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r7.claim: To explain a singular lamp and niche with plural houses, one answer is a shifting address that begins in the singular and ends in the plural, as at 65:1; another is that each individual house is intended; a third compares it to the moon placed “in them” at 71:16 though it is in only one of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r7.anchor: هذا من الخطاب المتلون الذي يفتح بالتوحيد ويختم بالجمع كقوله تعالى: يأيها النبي إذا طلقتم النسآء

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r8.claim: The first of five views identifies the houses as mosques set apart for worship, whose light shines for heaven’s people as stars shine for earth’s people.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r8.anchor: الأول: أنها المساجد المخصوصة لله تعالى بالعبادة، وأنها تضيء لأهل السماء كما تضيء النجوم لأهل الأرض قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r9.claim: A second view attributed to al-Hasan identifies the houses as those of Jerusalem.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r9.anchor: الثاني: هي بيوت بيت المقدس عن الحسن أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r10.claim: A third view attributed to Mujahid identifies the houses as the Prophet’s homes.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r10.anchor: الثالث: بيوت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن مجاهد أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r11.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r11.claim: A fourth view, from ʿIkrima, identifies them as houses in general.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r11.anchor: الرابع: هي البيوت كلها قاله عكرمة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r12.speaker: ابن بريدة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r12.claim: A fifth view identifies four mosques built only by prophets: the Kaʿba, the house at Jericho, the mosque of Medina, and the mosque of Quba.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r12.anchor: أنها المساجد الأربعة التي لم يبنها إلا نبي: الكعبة وبيت أريحا ومسجد المدينة ومسجد قباء قاله ابن بريدة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r13.claim: The mention of glorifying God morning and evening supports the view that the houses are mosques; al-Qurtubi prefers the first view, citing Anas’s report from the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37/r13.anchor: الأظهر القول الأول لما رواه أنس بن مالك عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that whoever loves God should love him, his Companions, the Qur’an, and mosques: they are God’s courtyards and buildings, blessed and protected, where worshippers pray and God attends to their needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r1.anchor: من أحب الله عز وجل فليحبني ومن أحبني فليحب أصحابي ومن أحب أصحابي فليحب القرآن ومن أحب القرآن فليحب المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r2.speaker: author
