QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r2.claim: Adhina means God commanded and decreed; its basic sense is knowledge and enabling without prohibition, strengthened when joined to command and execution.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r2.anchor: معناه أمر وقضى. وحقيقة الإذن العلم والتمكين دون حظر

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r3.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r3.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima take “be raised” to mean built and elevated, as in the verse about Abraham raising the foundations of the House.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r3.anchor: قيل: معناه تبنى وتعلى قاله مجاهد وعكرمة. ومنه قوله تعالى: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r4.claim: A Prophetic report promises that whoever builds a mosque with his own money will have a house built for him in Paradise; many reports encourage building mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r4.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى أحاديث كثيرة تحض على بنيان المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r5.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri and others take “be raised” to mean revered and honored, with mosques’ status elevated and their filth removed.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r5.anchor: يرفع شأنها، وتطهر من الأنجاس والأقذار

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r6.claim: A report likens a mosque shrinking away from impurity to skin shrinking from fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r6.anchor: المسجد لينزوي من النجاسة كما ينزوي الجلد من النار

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r7.claim: Ibn Majah transmits from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri that whoever removes harm from a mosque will have a house built for him in Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r7.anchor: وروى ابن ماجه في سننه عن أبي سعيد الخدري

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r8.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r8.claim: ʿAʾisha reports that the Prophet ordered mosques to be established in residential areas, cleaned, and perfumed.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r8.anchor: وروي عن عائشة قالت: أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن نتخذ المساجد في الدور وأن تطهر وتطيب

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r9.claim: Scholars differ over decorating and carving mosques: some disapprove, while others permit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r9.anchor: إن المراد بنيانها فهل تزين وتنقش

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r10.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r10.claim: Abu Dawud transmits from Anas that the Hour will not come until people boast about their mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r10.anchor: روى حماد بن سلمة عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن أنس وقتادة عن أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r11.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r11.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Anas’s statement that people will boast about mosques and then maintain them only a little.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r11.anchor: يتباهون بها ثم لا يعمرونها إلا قليلا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas predicts that people will adorn mosques as Jews and Christians adorned theirs.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r13.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r13.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim’s Nawadir al-Usul from Abu al-Dardaʾ warns that decorating mosques and adorning Qur’ans will bring ruin.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36/r13.anchor: من حديث أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r1.claim: Those permitting decoration argue that it honors mosques, as they understand “be raised” here to mean “be honored.”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r1.anchor: احتج من أباح ذلك بأن فيه تعظيم المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r2.speaker: عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r2.claim: It is reported that ʿUthman built the Prophet’s mosque with teak and made it handsome.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن عثمان أنه بنى مسجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالساج وحسنه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa permits decorating mosques with gold wash.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: لا بأس بنقش المساجد بماء الذهب

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r4.claim: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAziz is reported to have lavishly decorated and developed the Prophet’s mosque while governor, before becoming caliph, without anyone objecting.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه نقش مسجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالغ في عمارته وتزيينه، وذلك في زمن ولايته قبل خلافته، ولم ينكر عليه أحد ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r5.speaker: الوليد بن عبد الملك
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r5.claim: Al-Walid b. ʿAbd al-Malik reportedly spent on building and adorning Damascus Mosque three times the revenue of Syria.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r5.anchor: وذكر أن الوليد بن عبد الملك أنفق في عمارة مسجد دمشق وفي تزيينه مثل خراج الشأم ثلاث مرات

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r6.speaker: سليمان بن داود
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r6.claim: Solomon son of David is reported to have built the Jerusalem mosque with elaborate decoration.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r6.anchor: وروي أن سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام بنى مسجد بيت المقدس وبالغ في تزيينه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r7.claim: As part of their veneration, mosques must be protected from foul odors, vile speech, and other such harms.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r7.anchor: ومما تصان عنه المساجد وتنزه عنه الروائح الكريهة والأقوال السيئة وغير ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r8.claim: A sound report from Ibn ʿUmar says that during the Tabuk expedition the Prophet prohibited anyone who had eaten garlic from coming to the mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r8.anchor: وقد صح من حديث ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r9.claim: Jabir b. ʿAbd Allah reports the Prophet prohibiting those who ate garlic, onion, or leek from approaching the mosque because angels are harmed by what harms people.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#2/r9.anchor: وفي حديث جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r1.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits from Anas a report depicting the world’s mosques as adorned white mounts at Judgment Day, led by their callers to prayer and imams and accompanied by their regular worshippers, who pass like lightning and are identified as the mosque-going, prayer-keeping community of Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r1.anchor: يأتي الله يوم القيامة بمساجد الدنيا كأنها نجائب بيض

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r2.claim: The general promise that only believers maintain God’s mosques supports applying the ruling to every mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r2.anchor: وفي التنزيل إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says that seeing a man regularly attend the mosque is grounds to testify to his faith, citing 9:18.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا رأيتم الرجل يعتاد المسجد فاشهدوا له بالإيمان إن الله تعالى يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r4.claim: Mosques are also to be protected from buying, selling, and other distractions.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r4.anchor: السادسة: وتصان المساجد أيضا عن البيع والشراء وجميع الاشتغال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r5.speaker: سليمان بن بريدة عن أبيه
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r5.claim: Muslim reports that, after a man called out asking who would find a red camel, the Prophet replied, “May you not find it; mosques were built for their purpose.”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r5.anchor: أخرجه مسلم من حديث سليمان بن بريدة عن أبيه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r6.claim: The Prophet’s response establishes prayer, remembrance, and Qur’an recitation as the normal mosque activities.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r6.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الأصل ألا يعمل في المسجد غير الصلوات والأذكار وقراءة القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r7.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r7.claim: Anas reports in Muslim that a Bedouin urinated in the mosque; the Prophet stopped people from interrupting him, explained that mosques are for remembrance, prayer, and Qur’an, and ordered water poured over the place.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#2/r7.anchor: وكذا جاء مفسرا من حديث أنس قال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r1.claim: The command that God’s name be mentioned in mosques from the verse supports reserving them for worship and remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r1.anchor: خرجه مسلم. ومما يدل على هذا من الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r2.speaker: معاوية بن الحكم السلمي
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r2.claim: Muslim transmits the Prophet telling Muʿawiya b. al-Hakam al-Sulami that mosques are not for ordinary human conversation, but for glorification, magnification, and Qur’an recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r2.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاوية بن الحكم السلمي

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r3.claim: ʿUmar rebuked a man for making noise in the mosque, asking whether he knew where he was.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r3.anchor: وسمع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه صوت رجل في المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r4.speaker: خلف بن أيوب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r4.claim: Khalaf b. Ayyub left the mosque to answer his servant’s worldly question, explaining that he had avoided worldly talk there for a long time and disliked breaking that practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r4.anchor: فقيل له في ذلك فقال: ما تكلمت في المسجد بكلام الدنيا منذ كذا وكذا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r5.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits from ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb, from his father and grandfather, that the Prophet forbade reciting poetry in the mosque, buying and selling, and gathering before Friday prayer; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan, and al-Bukhari, Ishaq, and others used it as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r5.anchor: روى الترمذي من حديث عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r6.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r6.claim: Some scholars disapprove of buying and selling in the mosque; Ahmad and Ishaq hold this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r6.anchor: وقد كره قوم من أهل العلم البيع والشراء في المسجد وبه يقول أحمد وإسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r7.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r7.claim: A report says Jesus found people trading in a mosque, chased them with his cloak, and called them sons of vipers for turning God’s mosques into markets, saying this was the market of the Hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r7.anchor: وروي أن عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام أتى على قوم يتبايعون في المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r8.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r8.claim: Some Shafiʿi colleagues disliked teaching children in mosques if it was paid, treating it as a kind of sale; even unpaid instruction was opposed because children may leave dirt and soil the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r8.anchor: وقد كره بعض أصحابنا تعليم الصبيان في المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r9.claim: A Prophetic instruction quoted here says to keep children and the insane from mosques, along with swords, legal punishments, raised voices, and disputes, and to perfume mosques on Fridays and place water vessels at their doors.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#3/r9.anchor: وقد أمر صلى الله عليه وسلم بتنظيفها وتطييبها فقال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r1.claim: Ali reports that Uthman removed a tailor from the mosque and attributed to the Prophet the instruction to keep craftsmen away from mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r1.anchor: قال: صليت العصر مع عثمان أمير المؤمنين فرأى خياطا في ناحية المسجد فأمر بإخراجه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r2.claim: Qurtubi calls the report about excluding craftsmen unpreserved because Muhammad ibn Mujeeb is abandoned, but says its meaning is sound despite the weak route.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r2.anchor: هذا حديث غير محفوظ، في إسناده محمد بن مجيب الثقفي، وهو ذاهب الحديث. قلت: ما ورد في هذا المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العلم من التابعين
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports that some Successors allowed buying and selling in the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r3.anchor: قال الترمذي: وقد روي عن بعض أهل العلم من التابعين رخصة في البيع والشراء في المسجد.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r4.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to have permitted poetry in the mosque in several narrations.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غير حديث رخصة في إنشاد الشعر في المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r5.claim: Against those who ban or freely allow all mosque poetry, Qurtubi prefers allowing praise of God or the Prophet, defense of them, exhortation, and ascetic verse, exemplified by ‘طوفي يا نفس’.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r5.anchor: والأولى التفصيل، وهو أن ينظر إلى الشعر فإن كان مما يقتضي الثناء على الله عز وجل أو على رسوله

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r6.claim: Qurtubi bars poetry containing obscenity, lies, false display, or even mere frivolity, while allowing clean neutral verse; mosques are purified of such low speech under this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36#4/r6.anchor: والمساجد منزهة عن ذلك لقوله تعالى: { في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع }.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r1.claim: The Prophet's judgment is that good poetry is good speech and bad poetry is bad; the hadith is also reported from Abdullah ibn Amr, Abu Huraira, and Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r1.anchor: ذكر الشعر عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: «هو كلام حسنه حسن وقبيحه قبيح»

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r2.claim: Qurtubi says Shafi'i followers ascribe this saying solely to al-Shafi'i because they apparently had not encountered the hadiths.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r2.anchor: وأصحاب الشافعي يأثرون هذا الكلام عن الشافعي وأنه لم يتكلم به غيره وكأنهم لم يقفوا على الأحاديث

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r3.claim: The Prophet says to tell someone seeking a lost item in the mosque that God should not return it, since mosques were not built for that; Malik and others use this against raising voices.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r3.anchor: من سمع رجلا ينشد ضالة في المسجد فليقل لا ردها الله عليك فإن المساجد لم تبن لهذا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r4.claim: Malik and others prohibit raising voices in mosques, including for learning; Abu Hanifa, his companions, and Muhammad ibn Maslama allow it for disputes and instruction, but Qurtubi rejects necessity and urges decorum or a separate place like Umar's al-Batiha.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r4.anchor: وهذا مخالف لظاهر الحديث، وقولهم: لا بد لهم من ذلك، ممنوع، بل لهم بد من ذلك لوجهين

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r5.claim: Sleeping in a mosque is permitted for a needy traveler or homeless person, male or female; reports cite the people of the Suffa and Ibn Umar sleeping there as a bachelor.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#3/r5.anchor: وأما النوم في المسجد لمن احتاج إلى ذلك من رجل أو امرأة من الغرباء ومن لا بيت له فجائز

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r1.claim: Al-Bukhari's chapter on women sleeping in mosques cites Aisha's account of a black woman accused of taking a necklace who had a shelter in the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r1.anchor: وترجم باب نوم المرأة في المسجد وأدخل حديث عائشة في قصة السوداء التي اتهمها أهلها بالوشاح

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r2.claim: It is said that Ata ibn Abi Rabah made his dwelling in the mosque for forty years.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r2.anchor: ويقال: كان مبيت عطاء بن أبي رباح في المسجد أربعين سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r3.speaker: أبو حميد أو أبو أسيد
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r3.claim: The Prophet taught that one entering the mosque should ask God to open the gates of mercy, and on leaving ask for His bounty.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r3.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي حميد أو عن أبي أسيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r4.speaker: أبو داود
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r4.claim: Abu Dawud's version adds greeting those present and invoking blessings on the Prophet before asking for the gates of mercy to open.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r4.anchor: خرجه أبو داود كذلك إلا أنه زاد بعد قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r5.speaker: فاطمة بنت رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r5.claim: Fatima reports that the Prophet asked forgiveness and for the gates of mercy upon entering, and forgiveness, mercy, and bounty upon leaving.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r5.anchor: وروى ابن ماجه عن فاطمة بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r6.claim: Another report from Abu Huraira prescribes blessings on the Prophet and asking for mercy at entry, then greeting him and seeking protection from Satan at exit.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r6.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r7.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports a mosque-entry invocation seeking refuge in God, His noble face, and His eternal authority from Satan; Satan then says the invoker is protected for the day.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r7.anchor: وخرج أبو داود عن حيوة بن شريح قال: لقيت عقبة بن مسلم فقلت له بلغني أنك حدثت عن عبدالله بن عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r8.speaker: أبو قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r8.claim: The Prophet commands a person entering the mosque to pray two rakas before sitting.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r8.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي قتادة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r9.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r9.claim: The Prophet asks Abu Qatada why he sat without first praying two rakas and repeats that entrants should not sit until they pray them.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#4/r9.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما منعك أن تركع ركعتين قبل أن تجلس؟» فقلت: يا رسول الله، رأيتك جالسا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r1.claim: Most scholars treat the mosque-entry prayer as recommended, while Dawud and his followers make it obligatory; Qurtubi rejects obligation because it would bar entry by someone in minor ritual impurity until ablution, a position he knows of no one holding.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r1.anchor: وعامة العلماء على أن الأمر بالركوع على الندب والترغيب. وقد ذهب داود وأصحابه إلى أن ذلك على الوجوب وهذا باطل

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r2.claim: A report requiring two rakas at home as well as in the mosque has an unsupported addition according to al-Bukhari; only Abu Qatada's Muslim report is sound, and Abd al-Haqq notes Ibrahim's sole known narrator and sole hadith.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r2.anchor: قيل له: هذه الزيادة في الركوع عند دخول البيت لا أصل لها قال ذلك البخاري. وإنما يصح في هذا حديث أبي قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r3.speaker: أبو هند
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r3.claim: Abu Hind recounts Tamim al-Dari bringing lamps, oil, and rope from Syria and lighting the Prophet's mosque; the Prophet praised the illumination and offered him a daughter in marriage, which Nawfal arranged.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r3.anchor: حمل تميم يعني الداري من الشأم إلى المدينة قناديل وزيتا ومقطا، فلما انتهى إلى المدينة وافق ذلك ليلة الجمعة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r4.claim: Ibn Majah transmits from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that Tamim al-Dari was the first to light a lamp in mosques.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r4.anchor: وروى ابن ماجه عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: أول من أسرج في المساجد تميم الداري.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r5.claim: Qurtubi explains that zaban is a rare name borne only by Sa'id ibn Zaban, and al-maqt is the plural of miqat, meaning rope, apparently a reversed form of al-qimat.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#5/r5.anchor: زبان بفتح الزاي والباء وتشديدها بنقطة واحدة من تحتها ينفرد بالتسمي به سعيد وحده

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r1.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r1.claim: Anas's report promises the mosque-lamp lighter angelic prayers and forgiveness while the light lasts, and a further reward for sweeping mosque dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r1.anchor: من أسرج في مسجد سراجا لم تزل الملائكة وحملة العرش يصلون عليه ويستغفرون له ما دام ذلك الضوء فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r2.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r2.claim: Scholars recommend illuminating the home where Quran is read, with extra lights in mosques during Ramadan.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r2.anchor: ويستحب أن ينور البيت الذي يقرأ فيه القرآن بتعليق القناديل ونصب الشموع فيه، ويزاد في شهر رمضان

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r3.claim: One explanation identifies the men who glorify God as those who watch His commands and seek His approval, undistracted from prayer and remembrance by worldly affairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r3.anchor: فقيل: هم المراقبون أمر الله، الطالبون رضاءه، الذين لا يشغلهم عن الصلاة وذكر الله شيء من أمور الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عامر وعاصم والحسن ونافع وابن عمر وأبو عمرو وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r5.claim: Abdullah ibn Amir, Asim in Abu Bakr's narration, and al-Hasan read the verb with fatḥa as passive; Nafi, Ibn Umar, Abu Amr, and Hamza read it with kasra as active, also transmitted by Abu Amr from Asim.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر عنه والحسن «يسبح له فيها» بفتح الباء

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r7.claim: With the active reading, رجال is the verb's subject and there is no ellipsis or pause at الآصال because the verb requires its subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ «يسبح» بكسر الباء لم يقف على «الآصال» لأن «يسبح» فعل للرجال، والفعل مضطر إلى فاعله

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says every occurrence of tasbih in the Quran means prayer, as indicated here by the morning and evening times.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة ويدل عليه قوله: «بالغدو والآصال»

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r9.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r9.claim: Most commentators take the phrase for the obligatory prayers: dawn means Fajr, while al-asal encompasses Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r9.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: أراد الصلاة المفروضة فالغدو صلاة الصبح، والآصال صلاة الظهر والعصر والعشاءين

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r10.claim: Qurtubi says he already discussed al-ghudu and al-asal at the end of Surat al-Araf.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r10.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في «الغدو والآصال» في آخر «الأعراف» والحمد لله وحده.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r1.claim: A Prophetic saying urges living as guests in this world, making mosques homes, softening hearts, reflecting and weeping, and avoiding futile building, hoarding, and hopes.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r1.anchor: كونوا في الدنيا أضيافا واتخذوا المساجد بيوتا وعودوا قلوبكم الرقة وأكثروا التفكر والبكاء

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r2.claim: Abu al-Darda tells his son to make the mosque his home and reports the Prophet saying mosques are homes of the pious, whose frequenters God grants relief, comfort, and safe passage over the bridge.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r2.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء لابنه: ليكن المسجد بيتك فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r3.speaker: أبو صادق الأزدي
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r3.claim: Abu Sadiq al-Azdi urges Shuaib ibn al-Habhab to cling to mosques, reportedly once the meeting places of prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r3.anchor: وكتب أبو صادق الأزدي إلى شعيب بن الحبحاب: أن عليك بالمساجد فالزمها فإنه بلغني أنها كانت مجالس الأنبياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r4.speaker: أبو إدريس الخولاني
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r4.claim: Abu Idris al-Khawlani calls mosques the gathering places of the noble among people.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إدريس الخولاني: المساجد مجالس الكرام من الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r5.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r5.claim: Malik ibn Dinar transmits a divine saying that God withholds punishment when He sees mosque frequenters, Quran companions, and Muslim children.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r5.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: بلغني أن الله تبارك وتعالى يقول «إني أهم بعذاب عبادي فأنظر إلى عمار المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r6.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r6.claim: A Prophetic warning describes people in the last age sitting in mosque circles to discuss worldly life and its love, and says not to sit with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r6.anchor: وروي عنه عليه السلام أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r7.speaker: ابن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r7.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says a person seated in a mosque is conversing with his Lord and should therefore say only good things.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r7.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: من جلس في مسجد فإنما يجالس ربه، فما حقه أن يقول إلا خيرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r8.claim: A compilation gives fifteen mosque courtesies: greet on entry, pray two rakas, avoid trade, weapons, lost-property calls, loud or worldly talk, crowding, crossing worshippers, spitting, idle gestures, impurity, disorder, and neglect of remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#7/r8.anchor: وقد جمع بعض العلماء في ذلك خمس عشرة خصلة، فقال: من حرمة المسجد أن يسلم وقت الدخول إن كان القوم جلوسا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r1.claim: Qurtubi says observing mosque etiquette fulfills its due and makes the mosque a refuge and shield from Satan.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r1.anchor: فإذا فعل هذه الخصال فقد أدى حق المسجد، وكان المسجد حرزا له وحصنا من الشيطان الرجيم.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r2.claim: An unattributed report says a mosque rose to heaven to complain to God because its people discussed worldly affairs inside it.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r2.anchor: وفي الخبر: «أن مسجدا ارتفع بأهله إلى السماء يشكوهم إلى الله لما يتحدثون فيه من أحاديث الدنيا».

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r3.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r3.claim: The Prophet lists signs of the Hour: a crescent seen as though it were two nights old, mosques used as thoroughfares, and sudden death becoming common.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r4.claim: The Hour report is transmitted through Abd al-Kabir ibn al-Muafa from Sharik, al-Abbas ibn Dharih, al-Shabi, and Anas; others transmit it from al-Shabi as mursal, while Abu Hatim calls Abd al-Kabir trustworthy and among the abdals.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r4.anchor: وهذا يرويه عبد الكبير بن المعافى عن شريك عن العباس بن ذريح عن الشعبي عن أنس. وغيره يرويه عن الشعبي مرسلا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r5.speaker: أبو موسى
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r5.claim: The Prophet instructs anyone carrying arrows through a mosque or market to hold their points so a Muslim is not injured.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r5.anchor: وفي البخاري عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r6.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r6.claim: The Prophet calls spitting in the mosque a sin and says its expiation is burying it.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r6.anchor: وخرج مسلم عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r7.claim: The Prophet counts removing harm from a road among good deeds and unburied mucus in a mosque among bad deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r7.anchor: وعن أبي ذر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r8.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r8.claim: Wathila reports rubbing away spit from a mosque carpet as the Prophet did; Qurtubi notes al-Faraj ibn Fadala is weak and the Prophet's mosque had no carpets, correcting that he spat on earth and rubbed it with his left sandal.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r8.anchor: قال: لأني رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يفعله. فرج بن فضالة ضعيف، وأيضا فلم يكن في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصر.

QASHANI:24:36-38/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r1.claim: The houses are spiritual stations in which God guides whom He wills to His light.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r1.anchor: أي: يهدي الله لنوره من يشاء في مقامات

QASHANI:24:36-38/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r2.claim: The stations are raised through God's permission, with their ranks elevated.

QASHANI:24:36-38/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r3.claim: Remembrance progresses through the stations: tongue and struggle and moral formation in the soul, presence and vigilance in the heart, secret-realization and witnessing, spirit's bewilderment in lights, then absorption and annihilation in the Essence.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r3.anchor: باللسان والمجاهدة والتخلق بالأخلاق في مقام النفس والحضور والمراقبة، والاتصاف بالأوصاف في مقام القلب

QASHANI:24:36-38/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r4.claim: Their glorification is purification, transcendence, unity, detachment, and individuation, through dawn's disclosure and evening's concealment.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r4.anchor: بالتزكية والتنزيه والتوحيد والتجريد والتفريد بغدو التجلي وآصال الاستتار

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r1.speaker: كثير من المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r1.claim: The phrase “in houses” requires an implied construction; many scholars supply “like a niche containing a lamp in houses.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r1.anchor: أن التقدير كمشكاة فيها مصباح في بيوت أذن الله

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r2.claim: Abū Muslim objects that placing the lamp in God-approved houses adds nothing to the parable, since it does not make the lamp brighter.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r2.anchor: اعترض أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني عليه من وجهين : الأول

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r3.claim: Rāzī answers that a lamp in clear glass placed in a mosque is grander and brighter, making the parable more complete.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r3.anchor: أن المصباح الموضوع في الزجاجة الصافية إذا كان في المساجد

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r4.claim: Abū Muslim’s second objection is that the niche, lamp, and glass are singular, whereas houses is plural, so one lamp cannot be in every house.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r4.anchor: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني عليه من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r5.claim: Rāzī replies that the parable describes a type, so lamps of that description occur in all such houses and illuminate them at night for worship.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r5.anchor: لما كان القصد بالمثل هو الذي له هذا الوصف

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r6.claim: A second proposed attachment makes “in houses” modify the preceding phrase about being kindled from a blessed tree.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r6.anchor: التقدير توقد من شجرة مباركة في بيوت أذن الله

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r7.claim: Abū Muslim attaches the phrase to “an example of those who passed before you”: the earlier people are prophets and believers, and their houses are mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r7.anchor: أبي مسلم أنه راجع إلى قوله : { ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم }

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r8.claim: On this reading, accounts of earlier prophets and believers identify their locations as prayer chambers, as in the accounts of the intruders and Zachariah.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r8.anchor: وقد اقتص الله أخبار الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام وذكر أماكنهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that the earlier example concerns people who disbelieved and coerced slave girls into prostitution, not houses approved for remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r9.anchor: اعترض عليه القاضي من وجهين : الأول

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r10.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r10.claim: Al-Qāḍī also says this passage is disconnected from the earlier passage because the light verse intervenes.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r10.anchor: أن هذه الآية صارت منقطعة عن تلك الآية بما تخلل بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r11.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r11.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī treats this as a new sentence: the implied command is to pray in houses God authorized to be raised.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r11.anchor: قول الجبائي إنه كلام مستأنف لا تعلق له بما تقدم

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj see no ellipsis, but fronting and delay: men of the described kind glorify God in the houses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.anchor: قول الفراء والزجاج إنه لا حذف في الآية بل فيه تقديم وتأخير

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r13.claim: An objection to al-Zajjāj’s order is that “in them” repeats “in houses”; Rāzī says added wording for emphasis is common and preferable to omission.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r13.anchor: قلنا الزيادة لأجل التأكيد كثيرة فكان المصير إليها أولى

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the houses as mosques; ʿIkrima says they are all houses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين قالوا المراد من قوله

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r2.claim: Rāzī prefers mosques: some houses cannot be described as divinely authorized to be raised, and remembrance and prayer aptly describe mosques.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r2.anchor: والأول أولى لوجهين : الأول : أن في البيوت

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r3.claim: One view restricts the phrase to four mosques: the Kaʿba, Jerusalem sanctuary, Prophet’s mosque in Medina, and Qubāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r3.anchor: المراد أربع مساجد الكعبة بناها إبراهيم وإسمعيل

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the house as the Jerusalem sanctuary, where ten thousand lamps are lit.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن هو بيت المقدس يسرج فيه عشرة آلاف قنديل

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r5.claim: The other view includes all mosques; Rāzī rejects limiting the verse to four without evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r5.anchor: والثاني : أن المراد هو جميع المساجد والأول ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mosques are God’s houses on earth and shine for heaven’s inhabitants as stars shine for earth’s inhabitants.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r7.claim: One interpretation is that “raised” means built, supported by verses about raising the heavens and Abraham raising the House’s foundations; Ibn ʿAbbās says God ordered mosques built.

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r8.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets “raised” as honored and purified from impurities and idle speech.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r8.anchor: ترفع أي تعظم وتطهر عن الأنجاس وعن اللغو

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r9.claim: The latter interpretation is preferable: the wording suggests houses existed before God authorized their raising.

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r10.claim: The phrase covers every kind of remembrance, preferred because the wording is general.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r10.anchor: فالقول الأول : أنه عام في كل ذكر والثاني :

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets remembrance of God’s name in the houses as recitation of His Book.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r11.anchor: أن يتلى فيها كتابه عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r12.claim: A further interpretation is that people should not speak there about what is improper.
RAZI-FULL:v24p4/r12.anchor: لا يتكلم فيها بما لا ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, read yusabbaḥu with fatḥa on bāʾ; others use kasra.

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.claim: With the passive reading the statement continues through the time phrases; al-Zajjāj explains rijāl as the answer to “who glorifies in them?”
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.anchor: مرفوع لأنه لما قال { يسبح له فيها }

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r3.speaker: أكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r3.claim: Most commentators understand this glorification as prayer.

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r4.claim: Some take the prayer to be all five canonical prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r4.anchor: فمنهم من حمله على كل الصلوات الخمس

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r5.claim: Another view takes the prayers as dawn and afternoon, said to be the initially required prayers before more were added.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r5.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على صلاتي الصبح والعصر

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r6.claim: Another reading takes tasbīḥ as declaring God free of what is unfitting in His essence and acts; Rāzī finds it more apparent because prayer and zakat are separately coordinated with remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r6.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على التسبيح الذي هو تنزيه الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r7.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, meaning late afternoon; ghuduw is a verbal noun and does not originally form a plural, while aṣīl is a collective noun.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r7.anchor: جميع أصيل وهو العشي وإنما وجد الغدو لأنه في الأصل مصدر

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r8.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses bi-l-ghuduww as the times of morning, or mornings.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r8.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) بالغدو أي بأوقات الغدو

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r9.claim: A variant is wa-l-īṣāl, meaning entry into evening; āṣāl follows the pattern of aʿtum and aẓhur.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r9.anchor: وهو الدخول في الأصيل يقال آصال كأعتم وأظهر

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the forenoon prayer is mentioned in God’s Book and recites this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس رحمهما الله إن صلاة الضحى لفي كتاب الله

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r11.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that whoever regularly goes to the mosque, preferring it to other places, receives hospitality from God like that prepared in Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r11.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r12.speaker: سهل بن سعد
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r12.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports a Prophetic saying that whoever goes to the mosque to teach or learn good is like a fighter returning with spoils.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r12.anchor: وفي رواية سهل بن سعد مرفوعا

RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: Razi uses “I seek refuge in God” to show how a few words lead to many inquiries across grammar and related disciplines.
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: في تقرير مشرع آخر يدل على أنه يمكن استنباط المسائل الكثيرة من الألفاظ القليلة

RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: In aʿudhu billah, aʿudhu is a present-tense verb, the bāʾ is a preposition of attachment, and Allah is either a proper name or a derived noun, according to the disputed analyses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: أعوذ نوع من أنواع الفعل المضارع والفعل المضارع نوع من أنواع الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: Knowing a species requires prior knowledge of its genus because the genus is part of its essence, and simple concepts precede compound ones; thus explaining the phrase requires defining and classifying nouns, verbs, and particles, then examining each relevant form and disputed derivation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: معرفة النوع ممتنع حصولها إلا بعد معرفة الجنس لأن الجنس جزء من ماهية النوع

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r1.claim: The verse is usually read as continuing the previous verse, with the niche's lamp located within houses.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r1.anchor: This verse is usually read as a continuation of the previous verse, meaning that the lamp or “lighted wick” is in a niche within houses

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r2.claim: One continuation reading takes the light to be kindled in the houses.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r2.anchor: or, similarly, that the light is kindled in the houses

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase begins a new sentence: God permits houses to be raised and His Name remembered there, where He is glorified morning and evening.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r3.anchor: It could also be read as a new sentence: “In houses that God has permitted to be raised and wherein His Name is remembered

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r4.speaker: many
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r4.claim: Many commentators understand the houses to be mosques.

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r5.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r5.claim: Others extend houses to mean all houses.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r5.anchor: while others extend it to mean all houses

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r6.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r6.claim: Other interpretations specify the Kaʿbah, Jerusalem's Holy Sanctuary, the Prophet's mosque in Madinah, or Qubāʾ mosque.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r6.anchor: or else specific places such as the Kaʿbah, the Holy Sanctuary (in Jerusalem), the Prophet’s mosque in Madinah, or the Qubāʾ mosque

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r7.claim: Raising the houses can mean their construction, their exaltation, or both.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r7.anchor: That the houses are raised refers to either the building of such houses, their exaltation, or both

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r8.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r8.claim: Many commentators take glorification here to refer to the canonical Muslim prayer, ṣalāh.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r8.anchor: refers to the Muslim canonical prayer(ṣalāh

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r9.speaker: Sufis
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r9.claim: Sufis read houses symbolically as human hearts illuminated by the remembrance of God's Name.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r9.anchor: houses is understood here by Sufis to be a symbol for the illumination of the hearts of human beings

STUDYQURAN:24:36/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r10.claim: The juxtaposition of houses and remembrance evokes 22:40's list of monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques where God's Name is much mentioned.
STUDYQURAN:24:36/r10.anchor: The juxtaposition of the general word houses and the remembrance of God’s Name is also suggestive of the different kinds of houses of worship mentioned in

QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r8.claim: Mosques are God’s houses: He permits people to raise their needs there and answer them, and gives mosques higher rank than other buildings and monuments.
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r8.anchor: المساجد بيوته - سبحانه - وإن الله أذن أن ترفع الحوائج فيها إليه فيقضيها

QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r9.claim: Mosques are houses of worship and hearts houses of will: worship leads to God’s reward, while aspiration reaches God Himself.
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r9.anchor: المساجد بيوت العبادة والقلوب بيوت الإرادة ؛ فالعابد يصل بعبادته إلى ثواب الله ، والقاصد بإرادته إلى الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r10.claim: He also says that hearts are houses of gnosis, spirits are sites of love, and innermost secrets are places of witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r10.anchor: ويقال القلوب بيوت المعرفة ، والأرواح مشاهد المحبة ، والأسرار محال المشاهدة

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the lamps in the parable as being in the houses God authorized to be raised.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r2.anchor: المصابيح في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī allows مِن to attach to تُوقَد, making the sense that the lamp is kindled from a blessed tree in the houses.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r3.anchor: قد يحتمل أن تكون (من) في صلة (توقد) فيكون المعنى: توقد

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r4.claim: The houses authorized to be raised are mosques.

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r5.claim: Abu Salih identifies the houses as mosques.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح، في قول الله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the houses are mosques, which must be honored and kept free of idle talk.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] «وهي المساجد تكرم، ونهي عن اللغو فيها»

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says this includes every mosque where prayer is performed, whether congregational or otherwise.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] «يعني كل مسجد يصلى فيه، جامع أو غيره»

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses the houses as mosques built for worship.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال: «مساجد تبنى»

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan also identifies these houses as mosques.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r9.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال: «في المساجد»

TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r10.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r10.claim: Ibn Maymun reports that Companions called mosques God's houses and said God owes honor to those who visit them.
TAB-FULL:v17p315#2/r10.anchor: قال: أدركت أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم يقولون: «المساجد بيوت الله، وإنه حق على الله أن يكرم من زاره فيها»

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r1.speaker: سالم بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r1.claim: Salim ibn Umar identifies the houses as mosques.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r1.anchor: عن سالم بن عمر، في قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال: «هي المساجد»

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise identifies the houses as mosques.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال: المساجد

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r3.claim: Ikrima gives a broader interpretation: the houses are all houses.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال: «هي البيوت كلها»

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers mosques because the following description of men praying there shows these are houses built for prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.anchor: لدلالة قوله: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} [النور: 37] على أنها بيوت بنيت للصلاة

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets God's authorization to raise the houses as authorization to build them.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: {أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] قال: «تبنى»

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r6.claim: Al-Hasan interprets raising the houses as honoring them for God's remembrance.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] يقول: «أن تعظم لذكره»

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the sense of building, the common meaning of raising houses and structures, as with Abraham raising the House's foundations.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r7.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندي بالصواب القول الذي قاله مجاهد، وهو أن معناه: أذن الله أن ترفع بناء

TAB-FULL:v17p319/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r1.claim: God authorized His servants to remember His name in the houses.
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: ثم قال: {ويذكر فيها اسمه} [النور: 36] يقول: «يتلى فيها كتابه»

TAB-FULL:v17p319/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains remembrance of God's name there as recitation of His Book.
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: ثم قال: {ويذكر فيها اسمه} [النور: 36] يقول: «يتلى فيها كتابه»

TAB-FULL:v17p319/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says reciting scripture is one form of remembrance, but the broader sense of remembering God is clearer and therefore preferred.
TAB-FULL:v17p319/r3.anchor: وهذا القول قريب المعنى مما قلناه في ذلك، لأن تلاوة كتاب الله من معاني ذكر الله. غير أن الذي قلنا به أظهر معنييه، فلذلك اخترنا القول به

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r1.speaker: عامة قراء الأمصار
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r1.claim: Most regional readers vocalize يسبح with kasra on bāʾ, making it an active verb whose subject is رجال: men pray in the houses.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r1.anchor: وعني بقوله: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال} [النور: 36] يصلي له في هذه البيوت بالغدوات والعشيات رجال

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r2.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir read the verb with fatḥa on bāʾ as passive and make رجال the subject of an implied verb.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r2.anchor: سوى عاصم، وابن عامر، فإنهما قرأا ذلك: (يسبح له) بضم الياء , وفتح الباء، على ما لم يسم فاعله

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the active reading with رجال as the verb's subject because the report about the houses is already complete without this clause.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.anchor: والقراءة التي هي أولاهما بالصواب: قراءة من كسر الباء، وجعله خبرا ل (الرجال) وفعلا لهم

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r4.claim: The men perform prayer in these houses in the mornings and evenings.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r4.anchor: وعني بقوله: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال} [النور: 36] يصلي له في هذه البيوت بالغدوات والعشيات رجال

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says every occurrence of tasbih in the Qur'an means prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «كل تسبيح في القرآن فهو صلاة»

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the morning and evening prayers as dawn and afternoon prayer, the first prescribed prayers, invoked to represent worship.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: ثم قال: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال} [النور: 36] يقول: " يصلي له فيها بالغداة والعشي

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says God authorized these houses to be built so people could pray in them morning and evening.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.anchor: عن الحسن: { يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال} [النور: 37] «أذن الله أن تبنى، فيصلى فيها بالغدو والآصال»

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r8.speaker: أبو معاذ
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r8.claim: Abu Muadh glosses the phrase as the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r8.anchor: سمعت أبا معاذ، يقول: في قوله: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال} [النور: 36] «يعني الصلاة المفروضة»

TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the day described from the houses passage through the turning hearts and eyes as the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] . إلى قوله: {تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار} [النور: 37] «يوم القيامة»

SULAMI:v2p52#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r1.claim: The mosques are places where needs are raised to God.
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : رفع فيها الحوائج إلي

SULAMI:v2p52#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r2.claim: On entering a mosque, clear the heart of every concern besides God; He set these houses apart for being raised and for remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : إذا دخلت المسجد فادفع عن قلبك كل هم سوى الله

SULAMI:v2p52#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r3.claim: Another report says needs are lifted from hearts so they become occupied with remembrance; the Prophet relates God’s promise to give the best gift to one occupied by His remembrance instead of asking.
SULAMI:v2p52#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ترفع الحوائج من القلوب وتشتغل القلوب بالذكر

TABRISI:24:35-36/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:35-36/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، الجبائي
TABRISI:24:35-36/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and al-Jubbaʾi say these houses are mosques; the Prophet’s statement is cited in support.
TABRISI:24:35-36/r12.anchor: وهي المساجد في قول ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد والجبائي ويعضده قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:24:36-37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r1.claim: Mosques are God's houses on earth, illuminating the people of heaven as stars illuminate the people of earth.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r1.anchor: المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض وهي تضيء لأهل السماء كما تضيء النجوم لأهل الأرض

TABRISI:24:36-37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r2.claim: One view identifies the houses as four mosques built by prophets: the Kaaba, Jerusalem, Medina, and Quba.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r2.anchor: قيل إنها أربع مساجد لم يبنها إلا نبي الكعبة بناها إبراهيم وإسماعيل

TABRISI:24:36-37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as the houses of prophets and, by extension, the Prophet's family.

TABRISI:24:36-37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:24:36-37/r4.claim: Asked which houses the verse meant, the Prophet said prophets' houses; he affirmed that Ali and Fatima's house was among the most excellent.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r4.anchor: أنه سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قرأ الآية أي بيوت هذه فقال:

TABRISI:24:36-37/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r5.claim: Tabrisi supports the household interpretation with the purification verse and the greeting to the People of the House.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r5.anchor: وقوله ورحمة الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت

TABRISI:24:36-37/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r6.claim: God's permission concerns raising the houses of prophets and successors; raising means honoring them, elevating their rank, and purifying them from sins and impurities.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r6.anchor: فالإذن يرفع بيوت الأنبياء والأوصياء مطلق والمراد بالرفع التعظيم ورفع القدر من الأرجاس

TABRISI:24:36-37/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r7.claim: An alternative takes raising the houses to mean bringing one's needs before God in them.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r7.anchor: وقيل: المراد برفعها رفع الحوائج فيها إلى الله تعالى

TABRISI:24:36-37/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:24:36-37/r8.claim: Mentioning God's name in the houses means reciting His Book there.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r8.anchor: أي يتلى فيها كتابه عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:24:36-37/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r9.claim: Another explanation is that God's most beautiful names are mentioned in the houses.

TABRISI:24:36-37/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك
TABRISI:24:36-37/r10.claim: The morning and evening glorification means performing prayer at dawn and in the evenings.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r10.anchor: أي يصلى له فيها بالبكور والعشايا عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك

TABRISI:24:36-37/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:24:36-37/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says every occurrence of tasbih in the Quran means prayer.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة

TABRISI:24:36-37/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r12.claim: Another view defines tasbih as declaring God free of what cannot be attributed to Him and affirming the fitting attributes of His wise acts.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r12.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالتسبيح تنزيه الله تعالى عما لا يجوز عليه

FARRA:v2p253/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r2.speaker: عاصم
FARRA:v2p253/r2.claim: Most readers use kasra on bāʾ; ʿĀṣim reads fatḥa, making رجال the subject of an implied verb, “men glorify.” With kasra the verb is directly for رجال.
FARRA:v2p253/r2.anchor: قرأ الناس بكسر الباء. وقرأ عاصم (يسبح) بفتح الباء. فمن قال (يسبح) رفع الرجال

FARRA:v2p253/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p253/r5.claim: في بيوت can attach to the lamp-in-a-mosque description, or to يسبح, “in houses men glorify Him.”
FARRA:v2p253/r5.anchor: فإن دخول (في) لذكر المصباح الذي وصفه فقال: كمثل مصباح في مسجد. ولو جعلت (في) لقوله (يسبح)

FARRA:v2p253/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p253/r6.claim: أن ترفع means the houses are built.

THALABI:v7p106#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p106#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p106#2/r1.claim: The phrase may attach the lamp to houses, or mean that it is kindled in houses, which most commentators identify as mosques.
THALABI:v7p106#2/r1.anchor: ذلك المصباح في بيوت ويجوز أن يكون معناه: توقد في بيوت وهي المساجد

THALABI:v7p106#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p106#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p106#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says mosques are God's houses on earth and shine for the inhabitants of heaven as stars shine for earthly people.
THALABI:v7p106#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: المساجد بيوت الله عز وجل في الأرض، وهي تضيء لأهل السماء

THALABI:v7p106#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p106#2/r3.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
THALABI:v7p106#2/r3.claim: Amr ibn Maymun says the Prophet's Companions held mosques to be God's houses and that God honors those who visit them.
THALABI:v7p106#2/r3.anchor: وقال عمرو بن ميمون: أدركت أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم يقولون: المساجد بيوت الله

THALABI:v7p106#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p106#2/r4.speaker: ابن أبي بريدة
THALABI:v7p106#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Burayda identifies four mosques built only by prophets: the Kaaba by Abraham and Ishmael, Jerusalem by David and Solomon, and the Medina and Quba mosques by Muhammad.
THALABI:v7p106#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي بريدة في قوله سبحانه في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع الآية. قال: إنما هي أربع مساجد

THALABI:v7p106#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p106#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p106#2/r5.claim: Anas and Burayda report that the Prophet identified the houses as those of prophets and affirmed that Ali and Fatima's house was among the most excellent of them.
THALABI:v7p106#2/r5.anchor: قالا: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه

THALABI:v7p107/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r1.speaker: الصادق
THALABI:v7p107/r1.claim: Al-Sadiq identifies the houses as the houses of the Prophet.
THALABI:v7p107/r1.anchor: الصادق: بيوت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

THALABI:v7p107/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r2.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v7p107/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the houses are Medina.

THALABI:v7p107/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p107/r3.claim: The author prefers mosques because the context describes houses built for prayer and worship.
THALABI:v7p107/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال بالصواب أنها المساجد لدلالة سياق الآية على أنها بيوت بنيت للصلاة

THALABI:v7p107/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r4.speaker: قائل
THALABI:v7p107/r4.claim: An objection asks why the niche and lamp are singular while the houses are plural.
THALABI:v7p107/r4.anchor: فإن قيل: ما الوجه في توحيده المشكاة والمصباح وجمع البيوت

THALABI:v7p107/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p107/r5.claim: One answer calls this a shift in address that begins with singular and ends with plural, as in the address to the Prophet followed by plural divorce wording.
THALABI:v7p107/r5.anchor: قلنا: هذا من الخطاب المتلون الذي يفتح بالتوحيد ويختم بالجمع كقوله سبحانه يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء

THALABI:v7p107/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r6.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p107/r6.claim: Another answer says the singular referents recur individually in each house.
THALABI:v7p107/r6.anchor: وقيل: رجع الى كل واحد من البيوت

THALABI:v7p107/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r7.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p107/r7.claim: A further answer compares the wording to saying the moon is in the heavens, although it is in only one of them.
THALABI:v7p107/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو مثل قوله سبحانه وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وإنما هو في واحدة منها

THALABI:v7p107/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p107/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses raised as built, comparing the phrase with Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the House.
THALABI:v7p107/r8.anchor: أن ترفع أي تبنى عن مجاهد نظيره قوله سبحانه وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل

THALABI:v7p107/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p107/r9.claim: Al-Hasan interprets raised as honored or magnified.
THALABI:v7p107/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: تعظيم، ويذكر فيها اسمه

THALABI:v7p107/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p107/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's Book is recited in the houses.
THALABI:v7p107/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يتلى فيها كتابه

THALABI:v7p107/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r11.speaker: قتادة وأشهب العقيلي ونصر بن عاصم الليثي وابن عامر وعاصم
THALABI:v7p107/r11.claim: Qatada, Ashhab al-Uqayli, Nasr ibn Asim, Ibn Amir, and Asim read yusabbaḥu with fatḥa on the ba and without naming the agent.
THALABI:v7p107/r11.anchor: قرأ قتادة وأشهب العقيلي ونصر بن عاصم الليثي وابن عامر وعاصم بفتح الباء

THALABI:v7p107/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p107/r12.claim: On the passive reading, men is supplied as the delayed agent; the pause falls at evenings. Other readers use the active, making glorification the men's action.
THALABI:v7p107/r12.anchor: والوقف على هذه القراءة عند قوله والآصال. وقرأ الآخرون بكسر الباء جعلوا التسبيح فعلا للرجال

THALABI:v7p107/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p107/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says every occurrence of tasbih in the Quran means prayer, as indicated here by dawn and evenings.
THALABI:v7p107/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة

THALABI:v7p107/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r14.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v7p107/r14.claim: Commentators understand the obligatory prayers: dawn is Fajr, while the plural evenings include Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha because asil covers them all.
THALABI:v7p107/r14.anchor: قال المفسرون: أراد الصلوات المفروضة، فالصلاة التي تؤدى بالغدو صلاة الفجر

THALABI:v7p107/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v7p107/r15.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever regularly goes to the mosque morning and evening, preferring it, receives a prepared welcome and reward in Paradise for each visit.
THALABI:v7p107/r15.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما من أحد يغدو ويروح إلى المسجد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r1.speaker: الزجاج، الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r1.claim: One parse connects في بيوت to the niche as a qualifier of the indefinite noun, as فيها مصباح qualifies it; Abū ʿAlī chooses it and supplies a pronoun returning to the noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه من صلة المشكاة على تقدير: كمشكاة فيها مصباح في بيوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r2.speaker: الزجاج، الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r2.claim: A second parse connects في بيوت to يسبح له, treating فيها as emphatic repetition; this works with the common reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r2.anchor: القول الثاني: أن (في) متصلة بقوله (يسبح له) ويكون (¬1) (فيها) تكرارا على التوكيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r3.claim: With the reading that has fatḥa on bāʾ, في cannot attach to the verb of glorification.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r3.anchor: من قرأ (يسبح) بفتح الباء لا تكون (في) من صلة التسبيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r4.speaker: غيرهما
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r4.claim: Other grammarians connect في to توقد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r5.claim: The author starts a new sentence describing believers' mosques: the prior parable concerns one niche and lamp, so plural houses add no useful description and conflict with the singular niche.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r5.anchor: والاختيار أن لا تجعل هذه الآية متصلة بما قبلها؛ لأن الآية الأولى في (¬6) ضرب المثل لنور المؤمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو صالح، مجاهد، مقاتل، عكرمة، الحسن، أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r6.claim: They take the houses to mean mosques, making the verse general to all mosques.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r6.anchor: وأما معنى البيوت: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد المساجد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mosques are God's houses on earth, shining for heaven's inhabitants as stars shine for earth's inhabitants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p287/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس فيما روى عنه سعيد بن جبير: المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض، وهي تضيء لأهل السماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r1.speaker: ابن بريدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r1.claim: Ibn Burayda restricts the houses to four mosques built only by prophets: the Kaʿba, Jericho sanctuary, Prophet's Mosque, and Qubāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r1.anchor: الكعبة بناها إبراهيم وإسماعيل، وبيت (¬1) أريحا بناه داود وسليمان، ومسجد المدينة ومسجد قباء بناهما النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-. وهذا قول ابن بريدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says these are houses of Medina, where prayer and remembrance took place when the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: هي بيوت المدينة (¬2). وإنما خص بيوت المدينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r3.speaker: ليث عن مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r3.claim: Layth reports from Mujāhid that these are the houses of the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r3.anchor: وروى ليث عن مجاهد قال: هي بيوت النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r4.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the houses are the houses of the prophets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r4.anchor: وقد روي مرفوعا أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قرأ هذه الآية، فسئل أي بيوت هذه؟ فقال: "بيوت الأنبياء"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r5.claim: The author prefers the first explanation, that the houses mean all mosques.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r6.claim: Muqātil explains أذن as God commanded.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r6.anchor: وقوله {أذن الله} قال مقاتل: أمر الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r7.claim: They say the houses are to be built, as in the verse about Abraham raising the foundations.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2)، ومجاهد (¬3)، ومقاتل (¬4)، وغيرهم (¬5): أن تبنى، كقوله تعالى: {وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد} [البقرة: 127]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r8.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets raised as honored or exalted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r9.claim: The implication is that obscene speech should not be spoken in these houses.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r10.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī parses أن ترفع as an adjective of the houses, with its pronoun returning to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p290/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: قوله ([أذن الله] (¬2) أن {ترفع}) صفة للبيوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r1.claim: Muqātil says God's name is mentioned there by affirming His oneness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r2.claim: The glorification in these houses means prayer to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r2.anchor: {يسبح له فيها} يصلى لله في تلك البيوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r3.claim: The commentators understand morning and evening as the obligatory prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p292/r3.anchor: {بالغدو والآصال} يعني الصلوات المفروضة في قول المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads يسبح with fatḥa on bāʾ; the prepositional phrase stands as subject, and رجال identifies the implied glorifiers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر (يسبح) بفتح الباء (¬2)، وهذا على أنه أقام الجار والمجرور مقام الفاعل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r1.claim: The lamp mentioned in the preceding verse is lit in houses, meaning mosques.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r1.anchor: أي: المصباح يوقد في بيوت، يعني: المساجد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r2.claim: God authorized the mosques to be built.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450/r6.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450/r6.claim: Ibn Mujahid, transmitting from his father, glosses “be raised” as “be built,” referring to the houses of worship.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450/r6.anchor: قوله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] ابن مجاهد عن أبيه قال: أن تبنى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r1.claim: Qatadah identifies the houses in which God's name is remembered as mosques.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r1.anchor: {ويذكر فيها اسمه} [النور: 36] سعيد عن قتادة قال: هي المساجد.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r2.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r2.claim: A report from Abu Dharr says that whoever builds a mosque, even as small as a sandgrouse's nest, receives a house in Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من بنى مسجدا ولو مثل مفحص قطاة بني له بيت في الجنة»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r3.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r3.claim: A report from Ali says that whoever builds a mosque from his own wealth will have a house built for him in Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r3.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسول الله: «من بنى مسجدا من ماله بنى الله له بيتا في الجنة»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r4.speaker: كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r4.claim: Ka'b says the Torah calls mosques God's houses: He honors the visitor who performs ablution well and visits one, since a visitor deserves the host's generosity.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة أن كعبا قال: إن في التوراة مكتوبا: إن بيوتي في الأرض المساجد فمن توضأ فأحسن الوضوء ثم زارني في بيتي أكرمته

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r5.claim: The morning period is the dawn prayer, while the evening periods are the afternoon prayers, noon and mid-afternoon.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r5.anchor: الغدو صلاة الصبح، والآصال العشي، الظهر والعصر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r6.speaker: author
