YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r6.claim: Other verses mention the sunset and night prayers and elsewhere name all five daily prayers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر في غير هذه الآية المغرب والعشاء وجميع الصلوات الخمس في غير آية.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.claim: Yahya gives two ways to construe the phrase: stop at “evenings” and begin a separate statement, “in the mosque are men,” or connect “men” as those who glorify God there morning and evening.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.anchor: وهذا الحرف يقرأ على وجهين: {يسبح له فيها} [النور: 36] في المسجد {رجال} [النور: 37]

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r1.claim: The parable is of the believer's heart and the light of faith and Quran placed in it; God's being the light of heaven and earth means people there find guidance by His light.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله لقلب المؤمن، وما أودعه بالإيمان والقرآن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r2.claim: The exegetes take مثل نوره as the light in the believer's heart.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r2.anchor: ثم قال: مثل نوره، يعني في قلب المؤمن. كذلك قال المفسرون.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r3.speaker: أبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba's father recited مثل نور المؤمن instead of مثل نوره; the report is transmitted through Ubayd Allah ibn Musa and Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas and Abu al-Aliya.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r3.anchor: وكان أبي يقرأ: الله نور السموات والأرض مثل نور المؤمن،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p197/r4.claim: مشكاة is a non-through niche; its مصباح is a lamp inside a glass vessel.

ELMALILI:24:36-38/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r1.claim: The houses are mosques; their elevation means both unusually lofty buildings and their being held in honor and reverence.
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r1.anchor: yani binâlarının diğer evlerden ziyade irtifâ‘ı

ELMALILI:24:36-38/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r2.claim: The preceding parable's niche, lamp, glass, blessed tree, fruit, oil, light upon light, and guidance are manifested in these mosques.
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r2.anchor: O mişkât, o misbah, o zücâce, o mübarek ağaç, o meyve, o yağ, o îkād, o nûr üstüne nûr, o hidâyet bunların içinde temessül eyler.

ELMALILI:24:36-38/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r3.claim: Morning and evening glorification means declaring and sanctifying God's name in the mosques.
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r3.anchor: Allah’ın ismini tenzih ve takdis eyler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r1.claim: The author connects “in houses” as an adverb to the verb “they remember.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r2.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r2.claim: Other interpreters attach “in houses” to “the light is in houses,” “lit in houses,” or “there are men in houses.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r2.anchor: “o nur evlerdedir”, “evlerde yakılan”, “evlerde ... adamlar vardır” şeklinde yapanlar da olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r3.speaker: cami diyen tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r3.claim: Some exegetes identify the houses as mosques.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r3.anchor: Evlerden maksat “camilerdir” diyen tefsircilere karşı haklı olarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r4.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r4.claim: A response to the mosque reading notes that Muslims’ mosques had no lamps when this verse came, and continuous mosque lighting began under ʿUmar; if sacred buildings are meant, lamps suggest monasteries and synagogues where Jews and Christians worshipped without idolatry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r4.anchor: bu âyetin geldiği zamanda müslümanların mescidlerinde lamba, kandil vb. yoktu, mescidin devamlı aydınlatılması âdeti Hz. Ömer zamanında başladı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r5.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr’s preferred representation compares groups of objects and relations, portraying people gathered to read, discuss, and reflect on the Qur’an as becoming illuminated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r5.anchor: burada, bir tek şeyin diğerine benzetilmesinden ziyade, bir grup nesne ve ilişkinin diğer gruba benzetilmesinden ibaret olan güzel bir temsil sanatı vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.claim: The Prophet says that a group gathering in a house of God to recite and study the Book receives tranquility and mercy, and God mentions them among those near Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.anchor: Bir topluluk, Allah’ın evlerinden birinde bir araya gelip Allah’ın kitabını okudukları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r7.claim: Calling the Kaʿba God’s house is metaphorical: God needs no house and no place can contain Him; it means a place dedicated to worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r7.anchor: Allah eve muhtaç olmadığına, hiçbir mekân O’nu içine alamayacağına göre bu sözün hakiki değil, mecazi mânasının kastedildiği açıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r8.claim: The Kaʿba is God's house because Muslims face it in prayer, circle it in ṭawāf, and reserve it and its surroundings for worship of God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r8.anchor: Allah’a ibadet etmeye tahsis edilmiş mekân” demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r9.claim: Any place used for worship belongs to God in that sense and can receive His light; worship, remembrance, and reflection illuminate any place, not only mosques.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r9.anchor: Allah’a ibadet edilen her mekândır, her evdir. Bir mekânda ibadet, zikir ve tefekkür o mekânda nurdur

BURHAN:v4p160/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p160/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p160/r3.claim: The passage gives two analyses of ʿasā’s tense: past in wording and meaning because hope arose in the present, or past in wording but future in meaning because the reported hope is to occur.
BURHAN:v4p160/r3.anchor: قال وعسى ماضي اللفظ والمعنى لأنه طمع وذلك حصل في شيء مستقبل وقال قوم ماضي اللفظ مستقبل في المعنى

BURHAN:v4p160/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p160/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p160/r4.claim: In the first construction, ʿasā takes an explicit subject and a verbal infinitive as its complement; it does not take a participial complement, which does not mark past time.
BURHAN:v4p160/r4.anchor: أحدهما ترفع اسما صريحا ويؤتى بعده بخبر ويلزم كونه فعلا مضارعا نحو عسى زيد أن يقوم فلا يجوز قائما

BURHAN:v4p160/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p160/r5.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p160/r5.claim: The Kufans parse the infinitive after ʿasā as nominative in apposition, but the author objects that it cannot be omitted and can be advanced.
BURHAN:v4p160/r5.anchor: وقال الكوفيون في موضع رفع بدل ورد بأنه لا يجوز تركه ويجوز تقديمه عليه

BURHAN:v4p160/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p160/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p160/r6.claim: In the second construction, the infinitive itself is ʿasā’s subject, as in “perhaps he will rise”; it then needs no accusative complement.
BURHAN:v4p160/r6.anchor: الثاني أن يكون المرفوع بها أن والفعل وهو عسى أن يقوم زيد فلا يفتقر هنا إلى منصوب

BURHAN:v4p160/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p160/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p160/r7.claim: In “perhaps your Lord will raise you,” rabbuka cannot be the subject of ʿasā because that would split the relative clause; in “perhaps you dislike,” the pronouns belong to the verbs, not ʿasā.
BURHAN:v4p160/r7.anchor: لا يجوز رفع ربك ب عسى لئلا يلزم الفصل بين الصلة والموصول بالأجنبي

BURHAN:v4p51/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p51/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر
BURHAN:v4p51/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Qāhir says that when a question is spoken, an answer usually omits the verb and gives only a noun; an unspoken question needs an explicit verb because its cue is weak.
BURHAN:v4p51/r1.anchor: وذكر الشيخ عبد القاهر إن السؤال إذا كان ملفوظا به فالأكثر ترك الفعل في الجواب والاقتصار على الاسم وحده

BURHAN:v4p51/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p51/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p51/r2.claim: The open-bāʾ reading of “men glorify Him” challenges that rule: it supplies the verb as the answer to an implicit “who glorifies Him?” question.
BURHAN:v4p51/r2.anchor: فيمن قراها بفتح الباء كأنه قيل من يسبحه

ITQAN:v1p287/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p287/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p287/r1.claim: A Ṣaḥīḥayn hadith praises a prophet with a beautiful voice who chants the Qur'an aloud, saying God listens to nothing as attentively.
ITQAN:v1p287/r1.anchor: من الأول حديث الصحيحين ما أذن الله لشيء ما أذن لنبي حسن الصوت يتغنى بالقرآن يجهر به

ITQAN:v1p287/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p287/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p287/r2.claim: Another hadith compares public Qur'an recitation to open charity and quiet recitation to secret charity.
ITQAN:v1p287/r2.anchor: ومن الثاني حديث أبي داود والترمذي والنسائي الجاهر بالقرآن كالجاهر بالصدقة والمسر بالقرآن كالمسر بالصدقة

ITQAN:v1p287/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p287/r3.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p287/r3.claim: Al-Nawawī reconciles the reports: quiet recitation is preferable when loudness risks showing off or disturbing worshippers or sleepers; otherwise loudness has greater effort and benefits listeners and the reader.
ITQAN:v1p287/r3.anchor: قال النووي والجمع بينهما أن الإخفاء أفضل حيث خاف الرياء أو تأذى مصلون أو نيام بجهره والجهر أفضل في غير ذلك

ITQAN:v1p287/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p287/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p287/r4.claim: A sound report from Abū Saʿīd supports restraint: during retreat the Prophet told loud reciters that each communes with God and must not disturb or outshout another.
ITQAN:v1p287/r4.anchor: ويدل لهذا الجمع حديث أبي داود بسند صحيح عن أبي سعيد

ITQAN:v1p287/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p287/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v1p287/r5.claim: Some recommend alternating loud and quiet recitation so the quiet reader does not tire and the loud reader can rest.
ITQAN:v1p287/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم يستحب الجهر ببعض القراءة والإسرار ببعضها لأن المسر قد يمل فيأنس بالجهر

ITQAN:v3p161#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p161#2/r1.claim: When either a verb with its subject or a subject with its predicate must be elided, prefer the latter, since the omitted subject equals the predicate that remains and the deletion is nearly no deletion; use the former if another reading supports it.
ITQAN:v3p161#2/r1.anchor: إذا دار الأمر بين كون المحذوف فعلا والباقي فاعلا وكونه مبتدأ والباقي خبرا فالثاني أولى لأن المبتدأ عين الخبر

ITQAN:v3p161#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p161#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p161#2/r2.claim: A reading with fatḥa on bāʾ supports parsing the phrase with an omitted verb and the following رجال as its subject; a parallel active reading does the same for يوحي إليك ... الله.
ITQAN:v3p161#2/r2.anchor: كقراءة ﴿ يسبح له فيها ﴾ بفتح الباء

NAHHAS:v3p139/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p139/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p139/r1.claim: One interpretation takes the verse as a command to pray in houses.
NAHHAS:v3p139/r1.anchor: قد ذكرناه وقيل المعنى صلوا في بيوت

NAHHAS:v3p139/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p139/r2.speaker: عاصم وعبد الله بن عامر والحسن
NAHHAS:v3p139/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, and a report from al-Ḥasan read actively; al-Naḥḥās supplies رجال as an understood subject, supported by Sībawayh’s parallel and cited verse.
NAHHAS:v3p139/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وعبد الله بن عامر ( يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال ) وكذا يروى عن الحسن وقد ذكر سيبويه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r1.claim: Judge a comparison by imagining both ideas before either was heard: which comes more readily, and which better shows the originator's intelligence.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r1.anchor: تنظر إلى حالهما في قوى العقل ولم تسمع بواحد منهما فتعلم أن لو أرادهما مريد واتفقا له جميعا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r2.claim: Paired examples such as stars and lamps, or drawn swords and lightning, show that reciprocal comparisons differ in how readily they occur to an untrained mind.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r2.anchor: أن تقابل بين تشبيه النجوم بالمصابيح والمصابيح بها وبين تشبيه سل السيوف بعقائق البرق وتشبيهها بسل السيوف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r3.claim: The moving mirror comparison is subtler because it requires noticing the sun's continuous motion and finding a mirror moved involuntarily under that motion.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r3.anchor: وأن حركتها دائمة متصلة ثم طلب متحرك حركة غير اختياريه وجعل المرآة صادرة عن تلك الحركة ومأسورة في حكمها دائما

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r4.claim: Repetition can make an originally fresh, finely detailed comparison commonplace, so its present ease does not reveal its original ingenuity.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r4.anchor: حتى يخرج إلى حد المبتذل وإلى المشترك في أصله وحتى يجرى مع دقة تفصيل فيه مجرى المجمل الذي تقوله الوليدة الصغيرة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r5.claim: Phrases like لا يشق غباره and وهو كالبرق are now clichés, though they were not commonplace at their origin.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r5.anchor: فإنك تعلم أن قولنا لا يشق غباره الآن في الابتذال كقولنا لا يلحق ولا يدرك وهو كالبرق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r6.claim: Even أما بعد was originally attributed to one person, though it is now an ordinary expression.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p165/r6.anchor: ومثل هذا وأظهر منه أمرا أن قولنا أما بعد منسوب في الأصل إلى واحد بعينه وإن كان الآن في البذلة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r1.claim: It is mistaken to infer from dictionary glosses that a figurative expression has no merit over a direct equivalent; figurative speech gains an extra semantic step by using one meaning to indicate another.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r1.anchor: وكان من المركوز في الطباع ، والراسخ في غرائز العقول أنه متى أريد الدلالة على معنى فترك أن يصرح به

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r2.claim: 'Much ash in the cooking pot' first denotes frequent cooking and then signifies hospitality, so it carries two indications; 'much hospitality' states the meaning directly and carries one.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r2.anchor: كما ترى من أن الذي هو معنى اللفظ في قولهم : هو كثير رماد القدر . غير الذي هو معنى اللفظ في قولهم : هو كثير القرى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r3.claim: A dictionary gloss lacks this advantage because its obscure term and its explanation share one meaning; there is no second meaning for the original expression to indicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p323/r3.anchor: لأن الفضل كان في مسألتنا بأن دل لفظ المفسر على معنى ، ثم دل معناه على معنى آخر .

BURHAN:v1p50/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p50/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p50/r6.claim: One parsing connects في بيوت to the lamp in the preceding parable and continues through ويذكر فيها اسمه, with the following men describing the houses.
BURHAN:v1p50/r6.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون متصلا بقوله ﴿ فيها مصباح ﴾ أى المصباح فى بيوت

BURHAN:v3p199/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p199/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p199/r7.claim: In a passive reading of يسَبَّح له فيها ... رجال, the implied question is who glorifies God; the structure repeats the verb, makes a dependent element central, and reveals its agent after suspense.
BURHAN:v3p199/r7.anchor: فإن التقدير يسبحه رجال وفيه فوائد

BURHAN:v3p199/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p199/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p199/r8.claim: Another parse treats يسبح as a substitute for يذكر, with له فيها as a fronted predicate and رجال as the subject, by analogy with 87:1.
BURHAN:v3p199/r8.anchor: وله فيها خبر مبتدأ هو رجال

ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.speaker: عبد القاهر
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.claim: Abd al-Qahir says explicit questions are usually answered with the noun alone, while implicit questions usually state the verb because context signals them less clearly.
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد القاهر حيث كان السؤال ملفوظا به فالأكثر ترك الفعل في الجواب والاقتصار على الاسم وحده وحيث كان مضمرا فالأكثر التصريح به

ITQAN:v2p323/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p323/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p323/r16.claim: “To be raised” means to be honored.

ITQAN:v2p323/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p323/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p323/r17.claim: Remembering God’s name in these houses means reciting His Book.
ITQAN:v2p323/r17.anchor: ﴿ ويذكر فيها اسمه ﴾ يتلى فيها كتابه

ITQAN:v2p323/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p323/r19.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p323/r19.claim: Al-ghuduw refers to the morning prayer.

ITQAN:v2p323/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p323/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p323/r20.claim: Al-āṣāl refers to the afternoon prayer.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r3.claim: The houses in which the lamp is found are mosques.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r3.anchor: هذا المصباح في بيوت، يعني المساجد
